reviewerSummaries.summary: The ULR format, the 11% regain and conditioned-mass formula, the standard atmosphere (27 ± 2 °C / 65 ± 2 % RH), the 7% conditioned-size retest rule, the rate-card amounts, the 2021-22 volume figures, the clause 7.8.2.1 report-content set and the CERT-In/DPDP dates are all correctly stated and correctly hedged — that part of the document is unusually disciplined. The failures are concentrated elsewhere: acceptance tests and NFRs that unconditionally demand a ULR on a unit the document elsewhere configures as non-accredited; three mutually incompatible record-retention defaults; an 18% GST rate smuggled in through a worked example; a signature design that lets a self-signed certificate pass as the legal target; and three verified standards constants (140 °C, 0.25%, 0.5%) that the document tells the developer to seed but never states.

Five authors have produced five mutually incompatible vocabularies, role sets and system-of-record decisions on top of an otherwise well-structured spec: Section 2 settles the terminology in §8.3 and forbids specific words in §8.4, and Parts A, C, D and E then violate it in the places that matter most (Lot vs Batch, Request Line vs Order Line, Approving Authority vs Authorised Signatory, sub-sample vs sub-unit, "job" and "test log" still in use). More seriously, the document contradicts itself on who owns the customer, invoice and receipt records, on when allocations and labels are created, on how many approval steps exist, on the OPEN-Q numbering scheme, and on which roles even exist — each of which stops the solo developer cold.

M1–M10 is unusually thorough on records discipline, immutability, blinding and report freezing, and it correctly identifies the many-readings-to-one-result problem in prose — but the physical silk hierarchy is modelled one level too shallow (a 20-bale consignment is asserted to be one grading lot, which the governing standard forbids), the weight-certificate arithmetic that settles money between traders is specified without a single formula or a single seeded constant, and the two rules that most constrain the domain (the 7 per cent conditioned-size discard, and evenness as counted stripes) are either absent from the requirement IDs or modelled backwards. The high-volume reality is acknowledged in the prose and then contradicted by the requirements: a mandatory staged photograph per sample, mandatory per-specimen selection, eight scan stations and a 20-second-per-lot typing target cannot all be true at 11,000 samples a year, and the one worked example the document says "must settle" the design is a job type that is 0.6 per cent of the unit's work.

M11–M22 is unusually thorough on the things most home-grown LIMS specifications miss — the retrospective impact engines, the enforced expiry and competency gates, the frozen-file rule, the honest refusal to state a tax rate, and the explicit "we have no CloudZoo documentation" statement. But it fails on four of the specific compliance points it was asked to nail: the Administrator can rewrite the permission matrix and therefore escalate its own rights, the audit-trail immutability requirement leaves TRUNCATE/DROP and trigger-disabling open and never says audit capture cannot be switched off, the pseudonymisation promise is factually impossible alongside the frozen-PDF requirement, and one gate (unauthorised-person entry) is described as overridable in M15 and non-overridable in M13. There are also several cross-module contradictions that would stall a solo developer on day one — wrong section cross-references, two masters for the tax rate and the SAC code, and an "Expired" batch state that quietly breaks the observation-date rule it is supposed to serve.

The entity model in Part 2 and the database design in Part 5 were clearly written by different people and disagree in ways that stop code being written: two table names differ outright, several named CHECK constraints reference columns that do not exist, three of the six state machines have no enumerated state list, and the flagship 7%-rule requirement (WF-74) has no legal transitions to execute. The concurrency and integrity story is the weakest part — gap-free numbering is required and simultaneously made impossible by DB-08, report issue is not guarded against an in-flight retraction, the file store has a 24-hour RPO behind a 15-minute database RPO, and the signing/timestamp design breaks its own SHA-256 chain; the 40-week phase plan is roughly half of what one developer needs.

The specification absorbs the gap analysis unusually well: all 33 Tier-1 Critical capabilities and all ten must-ask questions have named homes (I verified each against the assembled SPEC.md, including renamed concepts — job to sample-test, blinding tiers, tokenised QR, batch impact analysis — and found no Tier-1 item entirely absent and no must-ask question without an OPEN-Q). The real damage is in §26 phasing, where five capabilities the gap analysis rates Critical (test request and contract review, equipment/lot/environment capture, report amendment and withdrawal, signatory and competency control, decision rule and uncertainty) are scheduled into Phases 2 to 4 even though Phase 1 goes live issuing signed certificates, in two cases contradicting the document's own [MUST] gates; separately, laboratory sampling and two of the twelve defined roles exist only as references with no requirement behind them.

Independently confirmed, and the defect is broader than the reviewer states.

1. The quote is verbatim. `parts/section_5_nfr_plan.md:655` (§26.4 Phase 2 Included) begins exactly "the Test Request Form with the recorded request review; enquiry and quotation; rate cards with customer-class and method-based pricing, ...". §26.1's phase summary table (L607) independently confirms the placement: Phase 2 = "Money: rate cards, **request review**, invoices, receipts...". So it is deliberate, not a prose slip.

2. Phase 1's Included list (L641) contains "sample registration including batch registration ... sample acceptance and rejection with a condition checklist and photographs ... the result-entry screen ... verification with send-back" and never mentions the Test Request, the order, or a request review. I searched for it under other names ("order", "TRF", "request review", "capability", "M3") in §26 — the only hits are L655 (Phase 2) and L477 (the `txn_order` schema row). Neither Section 2 nor Section 3 contains the word "Phase" at all, so there is no phasing caveat anywhere that softens the [MUST] gates.

3. The conflict is real and is a hard stop, not a stylistic one:
   - WF-1 [MUST] (section_2_workflow.md:251) — no sample may be accepted and no testing may start against a Test Request not in state Accepted; the Request Review record must exist before acceptance.
   - WF-31 [MUST] (L644) — the reviewer truncated this one; it actually reads "...or as a walk-in registration that immediately creates a Test Request and forces the Request Review before acceptance." The full text makes the finding *stronger*, not weaker: even the walk-in path mandates the request shell plus the review, so there is no Phase-1-compatible route.
   - M2-23 [MUST] (section_3_functional_core.md:292) settles which half belongs in Phase 2: "Enquiry and quotation are optional in the workflow... The capability check is never skipped; only the quotation is." The document itself says the enquiry/quotation may be deferred and the request-stage capability check may not.
   - Schema: `txn_sample.order_id` (L477) carries no NULL marker while sibling columns do (`customer_id NULL`, `subsample_id NULL`), i.e. NOT NULL. Phase 1 sample registration cannot insert a row without `txn_order`.

4. The equipment/consumable half of the finding also confirms, and there are two further instances the reviewer missed:
   - WF-14 [MUST] (L264) and WF-63 [MUST] (L672) require calibration and intermediate-check validity at Result Entered and at allocation; M7-12 items (d) and (f) (section_3_functional_core.md:1042) require the same at verification. Result entry and verification are Phase 1; the equipment and lot registers are Phase 3 (L667), with the equipment list and open lots not even migrated until Phase 3 (L720, L722).
   - **Missed instance A — competency.** WF-76 [MUST] (L685) requires the verifier to hold a valid Competency for that method version on the verification date, and DB-32 (L~578) enforces it as a trigger on observations. "the personnel register; and the competency authorisation matrix" is in Phase 3 (L667), migrated in Phase 3 (L723).
   - **Missed instance B — §26.3 contradicts itself.** Phase 1's own requirement list (L643) demands "DB-01 to DB-42". That range includes DB-30 (trigger: no observation against equipment whose calibration expired at `observed_at`), DB-31 (expired/unapproved consumable lot) and DB-32 (competency) — all of which need registers §26.5 defers to Phase 3. The same range also over-reaches the other way: DB-36, DB-37 and DB-40 are invoice/payment/refund-voucher constraints whose tables arrive in Phase 2, DB-39 needs the complaint register (Phase 4) and DB-42 needs `txn_qc_affected_test` (Phase 4). So Phase 1 is internally inconsistent on its own terms, independent of Section 2.

5. Severity: Blocker upheld. If Phase 1 is built as written, go-live accepts samples with no Accepted Test Request and no Request Review and records results against instruments with no calibration record — breaching the clause 7.1 and 6.4/6.6 controls that an assessor tests first — and the stated acceptance milestone ("one full day's real intake") cannot pass. It also invalidates the 12/6/5-week split and the cut-over plan the customer signs off.

6. The proposed fix is directionally right but incomplete and slightly wrong in one place: it says to "leave ... intermediate checks ... in Phase 3", yet WF-63 and M7-12(d) require intermediate-check validity at allocation and verification, so the validity date must come forward with the calibration date; and it omits competency entirely (WF-76, DB-32) and the Phase 3 de-duplication and the DB-range correction. Corrected fix supplied.

confirmed.location: section_2_workflow.md WF-80/WF-81 (lines 689-690), step 17 (line 33); section_5_nfr_plan.md §25.6 (lines 574-591)
confirmed.quote: **Verified → In Test** (retract) is permitted only while the allocation has not been reported, requires Unit Incharge authority and a reason, and archives the verified result as a revision.
confirmed.problem: A draft report freezes `txn_report_test.snapshot_json` at compile (step 17), but WF-81 says an allocation only becomes Reported "as a consequence of a report reaching Issued". So between compile and issue — which spans the Approving Authority's signature queue and, with WF-5 switched on, a payment hold of arbitrary length — the allocation is still Verified and WF-80 therefore permits it to be retracted to In Test and its readings changed. Nothing in §25.6 guards report issue against this: there is no rule that every allocation on a report must still be Verified at the moment of issue, no state or lock reserving an allocation to a draft report, and no re-check of the snapshot against live values. The system will happily issue a signed, numbered, ULR-bearing report containing values the tester has since revised, and the audit trail will show the revision as pre-dating the issue. This is the single most damaging integrity hole in the document.
confirmed.fix: Drop the new allocation state; use machinery the document already has. (a) Add to §25.6: "DB-43 | A report cannot move to Authorised or to Issued if any allocation it covers is not in state Verified at that moment, or if any of that allocation's current results carries a `rev_no` higher than the one frozen in `txn_report_test.snapshot_json`. | Trigger on both the report-authorisation and the report-issue transitions, re-reading `txn_sample_test.state` and `txn_result.rev_no` (where `is_current`) for every row of `txn_report_test`, and raising an error naming the offending allocation and its report number." The authorisation checkpoint is the load-bearing one, because M8-42 allocates the report number and ULR, renders the file, computes the checksum and applies the signature all at authorisation. (b) Amend DB-21 and the `txn_report_test` row in §25.4 so that `snapshot_json` additionally freezes, per result, the `txn_result.id` and its `rev_no` — without this DB-43 has nothing to compare against, since rev_no is not a printed value. (c) Amend WF-80 to: "**Verified → In Test** (retract) is permitted only while the allocation has not been reported, requires Unit Incharge authority and a reason, and archives the verified result as a revision. Where the allocation appears on any report not yet Issued, the retraction automatically returns that report to Draft, marks its snapshot stale so it must be recompiled before it can be submitted for authorisation again, names the report number to the retracting user, and notifies the report writer and the signatory." Acceptance check: "Compile a draft covering a verified allocation, submit it for authorisation, then retract that allocation. The report drops back to Draft with its snapshot marked stale, the signatory is notified, and authorisation is refused until the report is recompiled." This reuses the PENDING_APPROVAL → DRAFT send-back transition already in the report state model, needs no new allocation state, and so leaves WF-4, WF-81, §9.2 and the original-plus-amendment case untouched. Optionally add an AC-level scenario in §27 mirroring the DB-43 acceptance check, since the existing AC table has no case for a result revised while a report is pending authorisation.
confirmed.verifierReason: Confirmed verbatim and confirmed as a genuine unguarded window. WF-80 (section_2_workflow.md:689) permits retract while the allocation "has not been reported"; WF-81 (line 690) makes Reported arrive "only as a consequence of a report reaching Issued"; step 17 (line 33) freezes all printed values at compile, corroborated by DB-21 (section_5_nfr_plan.md:563), the txn_report_test row (line 490) and the research brief's compile transition (research_lims_reference.md:164, "never re-query live data later"). I searched for the guard under every plausible name — reserve/reserved, lock, recompile, stale, "still Verified", pre-issue, "affected report", draft-report handling — and it is absent. The only issue-time re-checks specified are DB-42 (QC breach), M15-28 (nonconformity withhold), WF-106 (accreditation scope) and M8-42's three checks (mandatory content, accreditation scope, signatory scope); none re-reads txn_sample_test.state or the result revision. §9.2's Verified row (line 605) offers no reserved/locked state and says only "Makes the allocation available to the report compiler". The document's own text confirms the window is long-lived, not theoretical: WF-6 says "Verification and authorisation proceed normally; only the final issue step waits", and M7-40 requires ageing alerts for verified work "awaiting authorisation longer than its own threshold". Retract (M7-37) → tester revises → re-verify → the stale draft is signed and issued: the allocation is Verified again, so no state check would catch it even if one existed, and M8-43/DB-21 guarantee the render comes from the frozen snapshot. The finding also survives the alternative reading that the freeze is later than compile, because WF-5's post-signature payment hold leaves a second window in which an allocation that is no longer Verified is carried to Issued/Reported. The proposed DB-43 references real columns (txn_result.rev_no and is_current exist at section_5_nfr_plan.md:485) and follows DB-42's existing "trigger on the report-issue transition" pattern, so DB-43 is a well-formed next identifier. The fix is imprecise on three counts, hence correctedFix: (1) the checkpoint is wrong — M8-42 performs number allocation, ULR allocation, rendering, checksum and signature all "on authorisation", so an issue-only guard fires after the certificate has already been signed and numbered; (2) snapshot_json as specified in DB-21 freezes "every value that is printed", and rev_no is not printed, so the rev_no comparison has nothing to compare against unless DB-21 is amended; (3) the new "Reserved for Report" allocation state is over-engineered and under-specified — it requires amending WF-81 and the §9.2 Verified row (the fix amends neither), risks contradicting WF-4 (invoice only for tests that "reached state Verified", raised at step 19 after authorisation), cannot represent a test that appears on both an original and an amendment draft (research_lims_reference.md:267 explicitly allows this), and depends on a draft-report "cancel" transition that exists nowhere in the document. Severity Blocker is justified notwithstanding the reviewer's rhetorical flourish: built exactly as written, the system issues a signed, numbered certificate carrying superseded results with an audit trail that makes the revision look pre-dated.

A developer implementing the banner from NFR-69 ships CANCELLED; from M9-14 ships WITHDRAWN. That is a concrete, testable conflict on an enum, so Major is fair.

Part C and Section 2 are internally consistent and clearly authoritative: WF-18 and L633/L634 of section_2_workflow.md, M8-51/M8-55/M8-59, M9-14, and the M8 field table at section_3 L1317 ("Report state | Draft / Pending approval / Approved / Issued / Superseded / Withdrawn") all use Withdrawn. front_matter.md L19 also says "genuine, current, and not amended or withdrawn". Section 1 and NFR-69 are the outliers.

WHAT DOES NOT STAND:
1. The M8-61 vs M8-62 sub-claim is a misreading. "Issued / Cancelled / Missing" is the established NUMBERING-SERIES state vocabulary, used identically in WF-99, WF-100, WF-102 (section_2 L773-776), M1-71, M1-72 (section_3 L176-177) and M17-37 (section_4 L882). M8-62 says "cross-checks the numbering series and flags any number that is neither Issued nor Cancelled" — that is the state of a NUMBER in a gap-free series, orthogonal to M8-61's report-status column. Section 2 §10.1's "A cancelled report keeps its number" is the same numbering concept. The two are legitimately different axes; no contradiction.
2. "The developer cannot enumerate the status column" is overstated. "One of the five states" at section_3 L1464 has an explicit referent 50 lines above in the same module: M9-17 ("Four distinct failure states exist", listing four) plus M9-18 ("A fifth, distinct state covers the report-substitution attack"). Five is traceable. It is imprecise (five signature-check states vs four M9-14 banners) but not unenumerated, and it is not evidence of a Cancelled state.

Adding "GENUINE — CANCELLED" and promoting Cancelled to a report lifecycle status creates NEW contradictions with at least five places: the M8 report-state field table (section_3 L1317) which has no Cancelled; M8-51/M8-59, which define exactly three post-issue mechanisms (amendment, replacement, withdrawal) and no cancellation; M9-09, which grants a verification token only to "every issued report version", so a cancelled (never-issued) number has no QR and the CANCELLED banner would be unreachable dead code; the M9-14 disclosure table (L1403-1404) and the M9 field table (L1475-1476), whose conditional rows cover only superseded and withdrawn; and it makes "five states" collide with the different five of M9-17/M9-18. Decisively, **WF-23 [MUST]** at L558 states: "The words in the table in 8.3 are used identically in the user interface, in the database table and column names, in printed documents and in all project correspondence." So this is a breach of a MUST-priority requirement, not a style preference.

4. THE WORD IS ALREADY TAKEN, WITH A DIFFERENT MEANING. This is the strongest point and the reviewer missed it. In this same specification "sub-unit" means a CSTRI branch establishment: `section_5_nfr_plan.md:430` lists `sub-unit` as a value of `mst_customer_category` alongside Reeler, twister, exporter and student; L655 refers to "the zero-charge advisory order type for in-house research and sub-unit samples". The research briefs use it only that way (`research_silk_domain.md` L36, L273, L284, L318 — "CSTRI's sub-units are grouped as STSC…"). Part C therefore overloads one word to mean both a bale of silk and a sister laboratory, in a document whose §8.4 exists precisely to kill that kind of overload.

5. THE GLOSSARY CONFIRMS IT IS UNDEFINED. `section_1_foundation.md:198` promises "Every term used anywhere in this document is defined here in one plain sentence." It defines **Sub-sample** (L295), **Bale**, **Book**, **Skein**, **Bobbin**, and prefers "sub-sample" over "Aliquot" — there is no **Sub-unit** entry.

I searched "specimen", "sub-sample"/"subsample", "bobbin", "draw rule"/"sample-draw", and regex combinations of per-reading x specimen across the whole 152k-word document: every specimen-to-test link is activity-level (M4-12's check is "Link ten bobbins to four allocations; each allocation shows the same ten bobbin identifiers"; M4-11 records the draw rule at sub-sample-creation level). Crucially, and missed by the reviewer, the data model confirms the defect and defeats the proposed fix: in SPEC.md 25.2 the txn_observation table ("Raw readings. Append-only.") has sample_test_id, parameter_id, reading_no, raw_value, uom_id, equipment_id, consumable_lot_id, observed_at, observed_by_personnel_id, entry_mode, source_file_attachment_id, is_excluded, exclusion_reason_id, excluded_by_personnel_id, supersedes_observation_id -- and no subsample_id. "subsample" occurs only twice in the entire data model: txn_subsample itself and txn_sample_test.subsample_id NULL, a single nullable FK that cannot even hold the ten bobbins the allocation-level multi-select promises. The acceptance check is therefore unimplementable against the specified schema, not merely unverified. The domain need is [F]-verified rather than inferred: parts/research_silk_domain.md:383 ("4 sizing skeins of 450 m from every bobbin = 40 sizing skeins. Each sizing skein weighed individually"), :385 ("20 panels from 10 bobbins, 2 panels per bobbin"), :399 (max deviation from the 4 coarsest and 4 finest, [F, S4]), and :428 ([F, S4]) which states the requirement outright: "each level generates its own readings. You need at least: lot -> sample_item -> test_run -> reading ... A flat 'sample has result' schema will fail on day one." Activity-level linkage is exactly the shape the brief warns against. One reviewer rationale is overstated and I discount it: computing maximum deviation from the 4 coarsest and 4 finest needs only sorted readings, not specimen identity. The per-bobbin attribution argument (deviant sizing skein -> which bobbin -> re-wind decision; attributing the 2 evenness panels per bobbin) is sound and carries the finding on its own. Severity Major is appropriate: it is one requirement, one table row and one schema field, not a structural failure of the spec, but it would be built wrong as written. The fix needs correcting because it leaves the schema untouched (creating a new requirement/data-model contradiction) and opens with an unconditional "Every reading row carries..." that clashes with its own conditional-mandatory clause and with M6-09's whole-sample visual and tactual ratings.

confirmed.location: M3, rules and edge cases item 4 (line 537); M2-06(e) (line 275)
confirmed.quote: The registration screen compares the quantity received against the sum of the minimum quantities of the requested tests and warns.
confirmed.problem: This contradicts M4-12 and M4 rules item 6, which correctly state that downstream tests share intermediate specimens: the 10 bobbins from the winding test feed size, evenness, tenacity and cohesion, and the same 20 seriplane panels serve evenness, cleanness and neatness. Summing per-test minima on a BIS grading order therefore demands several times the material the work actually consumes, so every grading job raises a false insufficient-quantity warning, the clerk learns to click through it, and the control is dead when a genuine shortfall arrives. The requirement also conflates two different masters: M1-26's per-sample-type "minimum quantity" and M1-29's "minimum chargeable quantity", which are a technical and a commercial figure respectively.
confirmed.fix:
Keep the reviewer's rewrite of M3 rules item 4 and the seeded draw rules (all [F]-verified at research_silk_domain.md:381, :382, :303, :107), but change three things.

1. Do NOT rewrite M2-06(e). M2-06 is a five-check, per-requested-test grid whose checks each render their own green/amber/red with a one-line reason and are stored per-check by M2-07; an order-level aggregate figure does not fit inside a per-test check and would re-contradict WF-34's per-test gate. Instead leave (e) per-test, restated to name its source: "is the requested sample type permitted for that test, and is the intended quantity at or above the technical minimum sample quantity on the test's Active method revision (M14-10) — not the minimum chargeable quantity of M1-29". Then add an order-level check following the M2-08 precedent, as M2-08a: "A seventh capability check covers material sufficiency for the request as a whole. The system resolves the sample-draw chains of all requested tests, deduplicates shared chains, sums only across independent chains, and compares the total with the intended or received quantity, flagging amber when short."

2. Reconcile the minimum-quantity masters rather than adding a fifth. Put the sample-draw structure in ONE place — M14-10 already declares "minimum sample quantity and the number of sub-samples or specimens" on the method version, so extend M14-10 with "and the specimen level the draw produces plus the method whose output it draws from, so shared specimen chains are resolvable", and make M1-36's "sample draw rule" a cross-reference to M14-10 instead of a parallel definition. Keep the reviewer's acceptance check, and add one for WF-34: "Receive 10 skeins against a full BIS grading order; Accept is available. Receive 3 skeins; Accept is unavailable."
confirmed.verifierReason: Confirmed. The quoted text exists verbatim at parts/section_3_functional_core.md:537 (SPEC.md:1782). The contradiction is real and stronger than the reviewer argued: (a) M4-12 (SPEC.md:1840), M4 rule 6 (SPEC.md:1922) and M1-33 establish that downstream grading tests consume shared intermediates; (b) research_silk_domain.md:429 marks this [F, S4] — "a test order for grading is a dependency graph with shared intermediates, not independent line items"; (c) research_silk_domain.md:381-389 show the draws sit at DIFFERENT specimen levels (winding 10 skeins to 10 bobbins; size deviation the same 10 bobbins to 40/80 sizing skeins; evenness 20 panels from those bobbins; cleanness and neatness re-use the same 20 panels; cohesion 10 test pieces from the same bobbins), so summing per-test minima is not merely inflated but dimensionally incoherent — skeins plus bobbins plus panels compared against a received quantity in skeins. confirmed.quote: Target entry speed for the dominant test: a trained tester must be able to complete the readings for **one lot in under twenty seconds** and a batch of thirty lots in under twelve minutes, excluding the physical weighing.
confirmed.problem: The target was written without reference to the number of readings, and for the dominant test it is physically unattainable. The research is explicit that the Limited test weighs twenty test skeins per lot to produce one lot result, so twenty seconds is one second per four- or five-digit weight including navigation — about five keystrokes a second sustained, against roughly 2.5 to 3.5 for trained numeric-keypad entry. The requirement's failure clause, "the target is met or the screen is redesigned", puts the developer on the hook for human typing speed, and no screen design can discharge it. It is also internally inconsistent: thirty lots at under twenty seconds each is under ten minutes, not twelve. The consequence of an unachievable [MUST] is that a real and important requirement gets waived along with the number.
confirmed.fix:
Align M6-41 with the document's existing authoritative numbers instead of inventing new ones, and leave the instrument import alone.

Replace M6-41 with:

"| M6-41 | Entry speed for the dominant test (Limited test, twenty readings per lot). The authoritative target is Section 1 goal 3 and success measure S3: a trained tester completes one lot's twenty readings in **under ninety seconds**, and a batch of thirty lots in **under forty-five minutes**, excluding the physical weighing. Because raw typing time is a property of the tester and not of the software, the obligation on the screen is the **overhead**: keystrokes and waits beyond the digits of the readings themselves must not exceed one keystroke per reading to commit and advance, and no more than three keystrokes to move from the last reading of one lot to the first of the next (per M6-40). | [MUST] | Time a trained tester on a thirty-lot batch and count keystrokes. The overhead limits are met, or the screen is redesigned; raw typing time is not treated as a defect. |"

Notes on scope of the edit:
- Delete the "twelve minutes" clause rather than reconciling it; the batch figure must be derived from the per-lot figure (30 x 90 s = 45 min) so the two cannot drift apart again.
- Do NOT touch M6-47. It stays [LATER], as OPEN-Q-T29 and the Phase 1 non-goal at section_1_foundation.md:344 both require. If import is wanted as a throughput lever, the right change is to add the volume rationale to the Phase 6 investigation OPEN-Q-T29 already schedules, conditional on the export actually existing.
- Optionally add a cross-reference from M6-41 to S3 so a future editor changing one is forced to see the other. Note separately that research_silk_domain.md:167 calls 90 s/sample too slow for 11,000 samples/year, so the 90 s figure itself may deserve review, but that is a distinct question and must be settled in S3 and goal 3, not by a divergent number buried in M6.
confirmed.verifierReason:

VERIFIED:
1. Quote is verbatim at parts/section_3_functional_core.md:924 (SPEC.md:2169).
2. Reading count is confirmed, not invented. parts/research_silk_domain.md:420 is marked [F, S10] (verified fact): "Twenty samples in each lot are weighed on a scale for finding out test results." -> 20 readings -> 1 lot result. The dominant test is the Limited test (parts/section_1_foundation.md:260: "about 98 per cent of Dharmavaram's samples"), and the spec itself ties 20 readings to one Limited-test lot.

THE REVIEWER MISSED THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE and substituted a weak argument:

confirmed.location: M9-04 (line 1369) against M9-02 (line 1367), M8-38 (line 1231) and the M3 report-grouping recommendation (line 528)
confirmed.quote: The payload carries, and carries only: a payload version; the issuing unit code; the report number and revision; the Unique Laboratory Report number where one exists; the report issue date; the sample identifiers; a very short sample description; the test or standard code; the fingerprint of the issued file; the fixed verification web address; and the issue timestamp.
confirmed.problem: The payload contents and the printed size are incompatible under the report grouping the document itself recommends. M3 defaults to one consolidated report per Test Request and the research's batch is 10 to 30 lots, so "the sample identifiers" means up to 30 numbers of the form DVM/2627/RS/00411 — about 570 characters before the description, the standard code, the ULR, the URL, the fingerprint and a 64-byte signature. That is roughly 800 encoded bytes, needing a version 25 to 30 QR symbol of 117 to 137 modules; at the 30 mm square M9-02 specifies that is 0.22 to 0.26 mm per module, below what a phone camera reads reliably off paper and far below what survives a photocopy or a fax. The payload also signs the verification address and then repeats it as the URL wrapper in M9-07, spending scarce capacity twice.
confirmed.fix:
Two corrections to M9-04, then a bounded new requirement.

(1) Amend M9-04 to: "The payload carries, and carries only: a payload version; the issuing unit code; the report number and revision; the report issue date; the number of samples the report covers together with the first sample number, and the last where the samples are a contiguous block; the first 16 bytes of the fingerprint of the issued file, rendered base64url; and the issue timestamp. It may additionally carry the two optional fields already required elsewhere — the headline result under the M9-06 configuration flag, and the opaque customer token permitted by M9-05 — and nothing else. The Unique Laboratory Report number, the sample description, the test or standard code and the verification address are not carried in the payload: they are printed on the report face, and the online tier returns them per ARC-20. The verification address in particular is already the URL wrapper of M9-07, and M9-37 makes the published address, not the encoded one, the trust anchor." The reviewer's version omits the M9-06 result field and the M9-05 customer token from a "carries only" list, which would put M9-04 in direct conflict with two MUSTs; the wording above closes that.

(2) Add M9-44 [MUST]: "The complete encoded string — the URL wrapper, the header, the payload and the signature — must not exceed 360 bytes, so the symbol is QR version 14 or lower at error-correction level M (73 modules). The build fails if any configuration can produce a longer string: the check must be run with the headline-result flag on and off, with the longest configured unit code, and with the largest sample count the bulk registration of M3-15 permits. The symbol prints at not less than 33 millimetres square, giving at least 0.45 mm per module."

(3) Amend M9-02's acceptance check from 30 millimetres to 33 millimetres so the two requirements do not disagree on the printed size, and extend it to: "Generate codes for a 1-sample and a 40-sample consolidated report, with the M9-06 flag off and on. All four are within the 360-byte cap and print at version 14 or lower; five different phones read each one first time from the printed original."

Why the reviewer's numbers must change. First, a 300-byte cap and "version 12 or lower at level M" are mutually exclusive: version 12 at level M holds 287 bytes in byte mode, and byte mode is forced because base64url contains lower-case characters. Second, the reviewer's own field list, encoded as a JWS with a 64-byte P-256 signature, a normal "kid", and the fragment URL wrapper, measures ~412 bytes — version 15 or 16, about 0.38 mm per module — so their cap is unreachable with their own list. Only after also shortening the host, the key identifier and every JSON key does a tight variant reach ~299 bytes, which is still version 13 (0.435 mm at 30 mm), and enabling the M9-06 result pushes it to ~332 bytes. The 360-byte / version-14 / 33 mm triple above is self-consistent (33 / 73 = 0.452 mm) and leaves room for the optional fields the other requirements demand. Third, use 40 samples rather than 30 as the stress case, because M3-15 permits 40 in one bulk registration. Finally, the reviewer's photocopy criterion should be recorded as a [SHOULD], not folded into a MUST: no requirement in the document currently asks the code to survive reproduction, so making photocopy legibility a pass condition adds a new requirement rather than repairing an inconsistent one.
confirmed.verifierReason: Confirmed independently. The quote is verbatim at parts\section_3_functional_core.md:1368 (SPEC.md:2613), and every supporting premise checks out: M9-02 (line 1366) fixes the printed square at 30 mm with the acceptance check "five different phones read it first time"; M8-38 (line 1230) defaults to one consolidated report per Test Request; the M3 recommendation (line 528) endorses that default because the work arrives in daily batches of ten to thirty lots; M3-15 (line 395) actually allows bulk registration of 40 samples of the same type and test set in one action; and the sample-number format is 17 characters (DVM/2627/RS/00411, line 514). I searched for a bound under every name I could think of (byte cap, payload size, symbol version, modules, capacity, error-correction level, "samples covered", "first and last", range) across all of parts\ and found none. The only nearby items are the technology choice in section_5_nfr_plan.md:342 (QR Code ISO/IEC 18004 at level M) and ARC-20 (line 362), which governs the separately published ONLINE record and notably carries a sample description, not the sample identifiers — so the online tier is not the source of the constraint. Measuring the actual encoding (JWS compact, ES256, base64url, as the research brief prescribes at research_india_commercial.md:477) makes the conflict concrete and in fact worse than the reviewer states: M9-04's exact field list with 30 sample numbers, a 64-hex-character digest, the ULR and the signed verification URL is 901 characters of JSON, 1,358 characters of JWS, ~1,386 bytes once wrapped as the M9-07 fragment URL. That is QR version 31 at level M (141 modules), i.e. 0.21 mm per module at 30 mm — not the reviewer's version 25 to 30. More damning, the ONE-sample case measures ~610 bytes, which is version 19 (93 modules, 0.32 mm per module), so M9-04 misses M9-02's acceptance check before the grouping question even arises. The research brief's own size budget (research_india_commercial.md:518, "roughly 300-380 bytes of JSON ... version 11-14 at level M ... about 30 mm square") assumed a SINGULAR sample id, no ULR, and offered "shorten dgs to the first 16 bytes" as a lever; the specification pluralised the field to "the sample identifiers", added the ULR and the revision, and dropped the size budget, so no requirement now carries the constraint that made the 30 mm figure true. The secondary point is also real: M9-04 signs "the fixed verification web address" and M9-07 then repeats it as the URL wrapper, and M9-37 makes the PUBLISHED address the trust anchor anyway, so the ~28 duplicated bytes buy nothing. This is a genuine buildability conflict between two MUSTs, not a misreading. Severity Major is right, not Blocker: the defect is confined to one requirement's field list, M9-02's acceptance check would catch it in test, and the repair is local. The proposed fix, however, is arithmetically wrong twice and creates two new contradictions, so it must be corrected.

confirmed.location: M10 lot header field table (line 1609) against M10-09's tare line 6 (line 1547) and M3-03 (line 373)
confirmed.quote: | Number of books per bale | Integer | Yes | One or more | Drives the tare scaling |
confirmed.problem: Number of books is captured once at lot level but consumed per bale: tare line 6 is "the tare of all the books in the bale", scaled by that bale's own book count. Bales in one lot do not contain equal numbers of books — the standard's own preliminary-examination proforma records "No. of books or bundles in a bale" per bale precisely because it varies — so a single lot-level figure mis-states the book tare, and therefore the net, oven-dry and conditioned mass, of every bale that differs from it. On a bale with 22 books priced off a lot figure of 25 the book tare is overstated by three books' worth, roughly 0.7 kg. Separately, M10 re-collects the bale count, the bale serial numbers and the book count that M3-03 already captured as sub-units on the sample, creating two sources of truth for the same physical facts with no rule about which wins.
confirmed.fix:
The reviewer's fix is directionally correct but leaves two dangling references and names a source of truth that does not yet hold the datum. Apply this instead:

1. In the M10 *Lot header* table (section_3_functional_core.md:1608), delete "| Number of books per bale | Integer | Yes | One or more | Drives the tare scaling |" and add in its place a derived row: "| Total books in the lot | Derived | Auto | Sum of the per-bale book counts | Prints on the certificate as the lot total |".

2. In the M10 *Per bale - weighing and tare* table, immediately above "Mass of the outer wrapper ('shirt')", insert: "| Number of books in this bale | Integer | Yes | One or more; defaulted from the bale's sub-unit row and editable with a reason | The multiplier for tare line 6; may differ from bale to bale |".

3. Amend M10-08 to make the per-bale basis explicit and testable: "...computes the tare per book from the sampled books, scales it to **that bale's own book count**, adds any bale-level components, and shows every line of the arithmetic. Bales in one lot may contain different numbers of books and the tare is computed independently for each." Acceptance check: "Register a two-bale lot with 25 and 22 books and identical packing-component masses; the two bales show different values for tare line 6 and for total tare, and each matches a hand calculation line for line."

4. Amend M10-29 (line 1585), which currently mandates that the printed lot identification block carry "number of books per bale" - a field that would no longer exist. Change that clause to "...number of bales, the total number of books in the lot, chop where supplied", and add to the Section II wording: "each bale row states that bale's own book count alongside its tare build-up."

5. Amend M10-05's acceptance check so a uniform lot no longer passes for the whole requirement: "Register a lot of four bales of twenty-five, twenty-five, twenty-two and twenty-eight books; the certificate shows four bale rows, each with its own book count, and a lot total of one hundred books."

6. Do NOT state that the book count is "read from the sample's sub-unit rows created at registration under M3-03 and not re-entered here" as written - M3-03 and the M3-16 field table (line 489-491) capture only a single "Number of sub-units" integer plus "Sub-unit serial numbers" marked not mandatory, and hold no per-bale book count at all, so the fix would point M10 at an empty source. Instead, first close that gap: add to the M3-16 field table "| Books or bundles per sub-unit | Integer | Conditional | Required where the sub-unit type is Bale or Carton | The standard's 'No. of books or bundles in a bale'; may differ per bale |", make "Sub-unit serial numbers" mandatory where the sample type is a raw-silk lot, and then add to M10-05: "The bales of the lot, their serial numbers and the number of books in each are defaulted from the sample's sub-unit rows and are not blind-entered; where the weighing-time count differs from the registered count, the difference is recorded with a reason, raises a nonconformity, and blocks the certificate until the Unit Incharge resolves it - consistent with the override discipline in M10-06."
confirmed.verifierReason: Independently confirmed. The quote exists verbatim at parts/section_3_functional_core.md:1608 (SPEC.md:2853) in the M10 *Lot header* block, i.e. one integer for the whole lot. Its consumer is unambiguously per-bale: M10-08 "scales it to the number of books in the bale", M10-09 tare line 6 "the tare of all the books in the bale", and M10-25 runs the whole gross-tare-net-oven-dry-conditioned chain per bale. I searched for a per-bale book count under every plausible name ("number of books", "books per", "books in", "book count", "books or bundles", "sub-unit", "n_books") across all five sections, the appendix and the front matter: the per-bale weighing grid (lines 1622-1639) has no book-count input, and the only other hits are "Number of books sampled for tare" (line 1627 - the divisor, a different quantity) and the group-level colour-group grid. So no per-bale figure exists anywhere, and the lot-level one is structurally the only multiplier available. Variance is corroborated by the document's own research, not merely asserted by the reviewer: research_silk_domain.md:244 gives Bale = "22-30 books, approx 60 kg" marked [F, S6]; line 251 records "No. of books or bundles in a bale" as a per-bale attribute of the Preliminary Examination proforma; line 210 states the standard's formula as n(M_p5 + 3M_c5)/5 with n the bale's own count; and cl.3.3 (line 257) requires the colour-group draw to be "proportional to the total number of books in each group", a rule that would be redundant under uniform book counts. Nothing in M10's 37 requirements or 8 edge cases asserts equal book counts per bale or provides an override. Both relevant acceptance checks (M10-05 "four bales of twenty-five books", M10-08 "matches a hand calculation") pass on a uniform lot, so the defect survives testing and surfaces only in production, on the one document the spec itself calls the commercial settlement figure. Two caveats that do not defeat the finding: the reviewer's magnitude is inflated (the spec's own example at section_2_workflow.md:392 is 1.6 kg total tare on 22 books, so three books is roughly 0.15 kg, not 0.7 kg), and the duplication half of the finding is weaker than the arithmetic half - within M10 the per-bale grid already derives "Bale serial number" as Derived/Auto, so the two-sources-of-truth issue is only against M3-03/M3-16 and is a reconciliation gap rather than a wrong number. confirmed.location: M1-49, M1-50, M1-51 (lines 118–120); no seed data anywhere in M1–M10
confirmed.quote: (c) the size category rule that decides which parameters apply
confirmed.problem: The grade engine is correctly declared to be configuration rather than code, but the configuration's content is nowhere specified, so nobody can seed it and the acceptance checks for M1-50 and M1-51 cannot be written. Missing entirely: the three size categories and their boundaries (Category I up to 2.0 tex / 18 denier, Category II 2.1 to 3.6 tex / 19 to 33 denier, Category III 3.7 tex / 34 denier and above); the rule that maximum deviation joins the major tests only in Category III; the rule that cohesion is evaluated only where the marked size is 33 denier or finer; and the fact that BIS maximum-deviation limits deliberately differ from the ISA values, so the two specification sets are not translations of each other. Without these, a developer will build a grade engine that applies cohesion to coarse silk and treats maximum deviation as auxiliary in all categories, producing wrong grades that look plausible.
confirmed.fix:
Adopt the reviewer's annex, with three corrections and one deletion.

Delete fix item (6). SPEC.md:5433 already states that BIS and ISA grade tables are entered separately "because they deliberately differ", and M1-49's acceptance check already creates them as separate records. Restating it in M1 adds nothing.

Add the annex to M1 headed "Raw silk grade computation reference data, IS 15090:2002, marked unconfirmed pending the scientist's grade tables", following the OPEN-Q-C11 pattern (seed the standard's values, mark each unconfirmed, require the scientist's sign-off against a real worksheet before go-live), containing:

(1) Size categories: I up to 2.0 tex (18 denier); II 2.1 to 3.6 tex (19 to 33 denier); III 3.7 tex (34 denier) and above. State that the category is resolved from the size **marked/declared on the bales**, not from the measured size, and add a cross-reference reconciling this with M6-03 ("declared or measured size") and WF-74 — a lot marked 33 denier may measure 34.5 denier and still pass the 7 percent gate, so the two clauses must not be left free to resolve the category differently.

(2) Major characteristics: size deviation, evenness variation I, evenness variation II, cleanness, average neatness, low neatness, plus maximum deviation in Category III only.

(3) Auxiliary characteristics: maximum deviation (Categories I and II only), evenness variation III, winding breaks, tenacity, elongation, cohesion.

confirmed.quote: **Scan stations** exist at, at minimum: receipt counter, store-in, issue to tester, bench / result entry, verification desk, report desk, retention store, and disposal or return.
confirmed.problem: Eight scan stations with eighteen mandatory custody event types and M4-23's requirement that every handover carry the receiver's own confirmation is a chain-of-custody design for a multi-room laboratory with a store keeper. This unit is three people in a shared room, doing 30 lots a day of a ₹50 test on material that never leaves the room. At eight stations that is roughly 240 scans and 30 separate receiver confirmations a day, on top of the 20-second-per-lot entry target — the two requirements are competing for the same clerk. The likely outcome is that scanning is abandoned wholesale and the custody log, which is the module's real compliance product, ends up empty.
confirmed.fix:
Leave M4-24 and its eight stations exactly as written. They cost one scan dispatcher plus an eight-row station-to-screen configuration table, sys_scan_event.station_code already carries them, Phase 1 scope (section_5_nfr_plan.md:641) already names them, and M4-20/M4-28/M4-29 [MUST] already require store-in and retention-store behaviour in Phase 1. Fix the grain of the custody event instead, at M4-23 and WF-50, modelled on M7-36's bulk-verification safeguards.

Add M4-23a [MUST]: "For tests flagged batch-custody in the test catalogue, one confirmation action by the receiving tester writes the issue-to-tester custody event for every sample on a worksheet, and one action by the returning tester writes the return-to-store event for every sample on it. One custody row is still written per sample, preserving the per-sample trail required by M4-27, M20-11 and NFR-106; each row carries the worksheet number as the authorising batch reference and the same receiver confirmation identifier. The batch action runs the M4-25 allocation and competency check against every allocation on the worksheet and is refused in full, naming the offending sample, if any one fails. Per-sample custody events with individual receiver acknowledgement remain mandatory for grading lots, conditioned-mass lots (M10), rejected samples, samples under complaint or dispute, and samples transferred to another unit or to a subcontractor; any such sample is excluded from the batch action and listed for individual handling, as in M7-36(c). Acceptance check: issue a 30-lot Limited-test worksheet containing one grading lot; one tester confirmation covers the 29 Limited-test lots, each of which has its own custody row bearing the worksheet number, and the grading lot is held for an individual per-sample confirmation."

Add M4-23b [MUST]: "Where the from-party and the to-party of a handover resolve to the same staff member — routine in a three-person unit where the receipt clerk also tests — the event is recorded once with both parties named and no second confirmation is demanded, since a person cannot acknowledge receipt from themselves. The record states that the parties coincided, so the overlap is visible to an auditor rather than disguised as an independent acknowledgement, consistent with the treatment of role overlap in M5-12."

Amend WF-50 to add: "Where the test is flagged batch-custody, the issue-to-bench and return-from-bench events for all samples on one worksheet may be written by a single confirmation action per M4-23a. The per-sample trail printed by M4-27 must still show both hops for every sample."

Add to the M4 rules and edge cases list, beside existing note 5: "A custody log that records thirty tester-confirmed handovers a day that did not physically occur is worse evidence than an honest batch record, because it is falsified. Match the custody grain to the grain at which the material actually moves — the worksheet — exactly as M7-36 matches the verification grain to the batch."

Also add worksheet_id (nullable) to txn_custody_event at section_5_nfr_plan.md:495, with a note that it is the batch authorisation reference and does not change the append-only rule of M4-21 or the entity_type/entity_id grain.

Combined with M4-23's receiver acknowledgement, that is 30 issue-to-tester confirmations plus 30 return-to-store events daily, in a shared room where the confirming tester is frequently the person who received the lot at the counter — a person confirming a handover from themselves, for material that never left the room. confirmed.location: M21, M21-31 (line 1482); M21.11 switch table (lines 1578-1627)
confirmed.quote: The audit trail shall be **immutable**: no user, no role, and specifically **not the Administrator**, shall be able to edit or delete an audit entry. Update and delete rights on the audit tables shall be revoked from the application's database account.
confirmed.problem: Revoking UPDATE and DELETE does not make a table append-only. TRUNCATE is a separate privilege and is not covered by DELETE; ALTER TABLE, DROP TABLE and ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER are not covered either. An account that can drop or disable the trigger required by M21-26 can then make silent changes with no audit row at all. Separately, nothing anywhere in the document says audit capture has no off switch — while M21.11 establishes a large configuration surface that the Administrator owns. As written, the single control the whole 7.5.2 case rests on can be turned off from a configuration screen or a database prompt.
confirmed.fix:
Amend M21-31 and align its two twins (NFR-105, DB-04) rather than replacing M21-31 wholesale. Reuse the document's own established two-layer pattern from M8-50 and DB-25 instead of inventing a new custody regime.

M21-31 [MUST]: "The audit trail shall be immutable: no user, no role, and specifically not the Administrator, shall be able to edit or delete an audit entry. Immutability shall be enforced in two layers, as for issued reports in M8-50. First, the application's database account shall hold INSERT and SELECT only on the audit tables; UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE and all schema-changing rights (ALTER, DROP, and the right to create, alter, disable or drop a trigger) shall be revoked from it, and the audit tables shall not be owned by the application account. Second, a trigger on each audit table shall raise an error on any UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE attempt, and shall record the attempt. Acceptance check: as the application account, attempt in turn an UPDATE, a DELETE, a TRUNCATE, an ALTER TABLE, a DROP TABLE and an ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER against an audit table; each is refused, and each attempt appears in the audit trail."

Add M21-31a [MUST]: "Audit capture shall have no off switch. No configuration setting, feature flag, environment variable or start-up option shall be capable of disabling audit capture in whole or in part, and the switch register in M21.11 shall contain no such entry. Removing, disabling or altering an audit trigger, or changing the set of audited tables, shall be possible only by a schema migration that is a change-control event under M21-57 and M21-58. Acceptance check: inspect the switch register and the configuration screen; no audit-disabling entry exists. Search the code and configuration for any flag that bypasses audit writes; none is found."

Add M21-31b [MUST]: "A daily audit-integrity job shall verify that every required audit trigger exists and is enabled, that the audit table privileges are as M21-31 requires, and that the audit trail has no gap: each audit row shall carry the SHA-256 fingerprint of the preceding row's key fields, forming a chain that the job re-computes, so that a removed or altered row is detectable even where a partition has been archived under M21-38. Any failure shall raise a System Incident under M21-52 and an immediate alert delivered independently to the Quality Manager and the Approving Authority as well as to the recipients of the SYSTEM_INCIDENT event in M19.1, and the alert for this event shall not be suppressible or re-routable through the notification configuration of M19-01. Acceptance check: disable one audit trigger in a test environment; the job reports it the same day and the incident and alerts are raised. Delete one archived audit row directly; the chain re-computation reports the break."

Two consequential edits, to keep the change consistent: (a) M21-37 remains as drafted, and M21-31 must not be read as forbidding the authorised retention disposal it and M21-64 provide for. State this explicitly by adding to M21-37: "Disposal of audit entries whose retention has ended shall be performed only by the separate, named disposal process of M21-64, using a distinct database account not reachable by the application, and shall itself create a permanent disposal record and preserve the chain of M21-31b across the disposed range." (b) Update NFR-105 (section_5_nfr_plan.md:243) and DB-04 (line 544) so their "How" columns carry the full revoked privilege list, the guard trigger and the row-chain column, rather than "No UPDATE or DELETE permission"; and add the six negative privilege tests to the M21.10 regression list beside existing test 8.

On credentials, replace the reviewer's "parent body in sealed custody" with something the document can actually sustain: add to M21-61 that the privileged database account capable of schema change on the audit tables shall be named in the infrastructure specification, its credential held under dual control by the Approving Authority and not by the Administrator or the developer in day-to-day use, and every use of it recorded as a change-control event under M21-57.
confirmed.verifierReason:
The quote is verbatim (parts/section_4_functional_support.md:1482; SPEC.md:4407), and the core technical claim holds up under search. Every statement of audit immutability in the document stops at the same two verbs: M21-31, NFR-105 (section_5_nfr_plan.md:243) and DB-04 (section_5_nfr_plan.md:544) all say only "no UPDATE or DELETE permission". I searched TRUNCATE, ALTER TABLE, DROP TABLE, DISABLE TRIGGER, revoke, GRANT, privilege, least-privilege and hardening across all five authored sections: none of those appear anywhere in a database-rights context. So an implementer can satisfy M21-31 literally and pass its stated acceptance check while the application login (normally the schema owner on the single-server deployment of M21-55) retains TRUNCATE, ALTER, DROP and the ability to disable the M21-26 capture trigger, after which changes leave no audit row at all.

The decisive corroboration is internal asymmetry, not the reviewer's outside reasoning. For issued reports, M8-50 (section_3_functional_core.md:1254) requires revoked permissions "and by a trigger that raises an error on any modification attempt", specified concretely in DB-25 (line 574). The audit table — on which the entire cl. 7.5.2 case rests (research_nabl_17025.md:279, item A5) — receives only the weaker half of that same pattern, with no guard trigger and no requirement anywhere that the capture triggers exist and are enabled. Nothing covers this gap under another name: M21-54 and NFR-42 verify file checksums and referential constraints only, and there is no hash chain or sequence-continuity check on audit rows anywhere in the document.

The severity is Major, not Blocker. M21-31's first sentence is an unconditional normative prohibition ("shall be immutable: no user, no role, and specifically not the Administrator"), reinforced by the permission-matrix note at line 1448, the read-only Audit Trail Viewer at line 1329, and regression test 8 ("Edit an audit entry as the Administrator - Refused"). The requirement therefore exists and binds; what is defective is the implementation clause that follows it, which enumerates an incomplete privilege set and so under-specifies a control the document elsewhere knows how to specify properly. That is a precision defect in a stated MUST, not a missing requirement.

The reviewer's second claim is overstated and should not carry the finding. I read the full M21.11 table (lines 1578-1627): it contains no audit entry, and no audit-disabling switch, feature flag or environment variable is specified anywhere in the document. M21-58 additionally places every configuration change under change control. So "the single control the whole 7.5.2 case rests on can be turned off from a configuration screen" is not supported by the text. The defensible residue is narrower: the document never affirmatively states that audit capture has no off switch, which is worth adding as hardening but is not by itself a defect.

The proposed fix is wrong in three specific ways and would introduce fresh contradictions. (1) "INSERT and SELECT only ... revoked from it and from every account reachable by the application or by the Administrator" contradicts M21-37, which contemplates a retention purge that must merely spare in-retention entries, and M21-64, which requires authorised disposal to produce a disposal record; the fix makes lawful, change-controlled disposal of expired audit rows impossible through the system. (2) "each audit table's row count is monotonically non-decreasing" contradicts M21-38, which partitions or archives the audit trail by month; a naive row-count check would raise a false failure at every archival. (3) "an immediate alert to the Quality Manager and Approving Authority - not to the Administrator" contradicts the M19.1 event table at line 1116, where SYSTEM_INCIDENT is defined as going to the Administrator and Lab In-Charge; and "Database credentials ... held by the parent body in sealed custody" invents an organisational arrangement the document nowhere supports and which would block the routine schema migration and patching that M21-61 treats as ordinary change-controlled infrastructure work.

confirmed.location: M21, M21-72 (line 1669) and the M21.12 retention table (line 1653), against M17-39 (line 884) and M22-20 (line 1752)

QUOTE VERIFIED. The text is exact, at SPEC.md:4594 and parts/section_4_functional_support.md:1669.

THE CORE CONTRADICTION IS REAL AND CONFIRMED. - SPEC.md:2539-2540: the report record itself holds "Customer name (frozen)" and "Customer address (frozen)", explicitly "Read-only after issue". So the name persists in the database row, not merely inside a PDF.
- M8-43 (2487), M10-35 (2836), M17-39 (3809), M22-20 (4677): the issued file is stored as bytes with a checksum, re-served from the stored file, and reprints must be byte-identical. M21-40 (4421) binds the electronic signature to the file or its checksum.
- M17-27 (3797) puts the recipient's name and address on the tax invoice; M1-05 (1284) and M1-15 (1299) confirm issued reports and invoices keep printing the frozen name.

SEVERITY DOWNGRADED FROM BLOCKER TO MAJOR. The reviewer's framing overstates the harm on two counts:

The defect is one overreaching clause plus a broken acceptance check, not a wrong architecture.
2. The reviewer's supporting claim about registers is FALSE. M20-18 requires that "A register print shall reflect the data as at the time of printing", and M20-01/M20-20 render the customer field as the pseudonym when identity is masked. The M20 registers are live views over the data, not frozen files, so a print taken after pseudonymisation shows the token, not the name. The name does NOT survive in the registers as the reviewer asserts.

THE PROPOSED FIX IS WRONG IN THREE PLACES and must not be applied as written:
(a) The replacement acceptance check asserts the "sample inward, test, report-issue and dispatch registers ... are unchanged and still contain the name recorded at the time of issue." That directly contradicts M20-18 and M20-20 and would silently invent a new requirement to freeze names into registers.
(b) The new retention row "Retention period of the document containing it (8-10 years)" contradicts the existing row "Sample inward, test, report issue and dispatch registers | Permanent", and also the "Life of the instrument plus 10 years" and "Audit trail" rows. For the equipment cause there is no equivalent at any level: negative tests 15 and 16 check only that the impact-analysis query "returns exactly the expected set", and no DB rule keys off `txn_ncr_affected`.

3. NO COMPENSATING GATE AT ISSUE. M8-42 (line 2486) enumerates the authorisation transaction — mandatory content check, accreditation scope check, signatory scope check, numbering, render, checksum, token, signature. No re-check of calibration validity. M11-19 / DB-30 are observation-time gates, so they do not touch already-entered results. M15-28's withhold is permissive ("shall **support** a Withhold report state"; acceptance: "**Set** risk to Critical with withhold"), i.e. an operator toggle, not an automatic consequence of M11-24 or M15-27. So a Verified-but-unreported affected test can be issued the next morning with nothing standing in the way. The reviewer's core claim holds.

4. WHERE THE REVIEWER OVERSTATES. "Forces a decision only on those already reported" is true of M11-24(c) but is contradicted elsewhere: AC-18 (line 5573) requires that "every test, sample and issued report ... each is dispositioned"; the M11.1 screens table (line 2941) says "disposition each" result and report; M11.6 rule 3 (line 3072) says "every result produced after that date must be dispositioned"; and `txn_ncr_affected` (line 5221) carries `sample_test_id`, `report_id` and `disposition`. Additionally M7-11/M7-12(d)/M7-13 make "the instrument used was In Service with valid calibration and intermediate check at the observation time" a system-pre-filled checklist item whose No blocks verification — partial cover for the not-yet-verified subset, though not for the already-Verified subset, and the spec never says a `suspect_from` retroactively invalidates a nominally-valid certificate. Net effect: disposition *scope* is an internal inconsistency (M11-24(c) narrower than AC-18), while the *withholding* gap the reviewer names is genuinely unwired.

5. NOT AN OVERSTATED FACT. `parts\research_nabl_17025.md` line 545 marks 7.10.1(b) as a real clause requirement and says "`WITHHOLD_REPORT` must be an actual system state that blocks issue, not a note". The brief's own §5.2 step 4 says "dispositions each affected report", so M11-24(c) faithfully mirrors the brief — the gap is inherited, but the clause the reviewer cites does support the finding.

6. THE FIX IS SUBSTANTIVELY RIGHT BUT IMPRECISE IN TWO WAYS. (a) It cites "the Withheld state of M15-28"; M15-28 defines a Withhold-report flag on the Nonconformity (`withhold_reports BOOLEAN` on `txn_ncr`), whereas the test-level Withheld state that blocks verification and report issue is M15-04. Worse, "Withheld" is not in the §9.2 Table B Test Allocation state list (Pending, Allocated, Awaiting Conditioning, In Test, Result Entered, Under Verification, Verified, Reported, Discarded, Invalidated, On Hold, Subcontracted, Aborted, Cancelled), so the state must be added there with a transition rule beside WF-87. (b) Applying the clause verbatim to M15-29 makes automatic withholding mandatory for every NCR impact analysis regardless of cause or risk — including analyst and method-version causes and Minor NCRs — which contradicts M15-28's risk-level-driven design and 7.10.1(b)'s "as necessary ... based upon the risk levels".

confirmed.location: M17-13 (line 853), with M17-24 (line 864) and M17-25 (line 865)
confirmed.quote: with a payment mode from: Cash; Demand draft; Cheque; Bank transfer (National Electronic Funds Transfer or Real Time Gross Settlement); Unified Payments Interface; Payment gateway; Government non-tax receipt portal challan; Bank collection product; Adjustment from advance; Waiver.
confirmed.problem: Two of these ten are not tenders of money. A waiver is a reduction of the charge (already an approval object in M17-10) and an advance adjustment is the application of money already receipted once. Recording either as a Payment double-counts collections: the Daily Collection Register will show cash that is not in the drawer, and the collection-versus-remittance reconciliation can never balance because there is nothing to deposit. In a government unit whose daily cash handover is signed for, this produces an unexplainable shortfall every time a waiver is granted — the kind of thing that becomes an audit paragraph.

Delete "Adjustment from advance" and "Waiver" from the M17-13 mode list, leaving eight money modes (no other requirement references either value; the M17.6 field table's "Mode | List (M17-13)" needs no edit). Then add:

M17-13a [MUST]: "Every payment mode in M17-13 is a movement of money. The Daily Collection Register (M17-24) and the collection-versus-remittance reconciliation (M17-25) shall be computed only over Payment records, and no non-monetary settlement shall ever create a Payment record, consume a Money Receipt number (M17-16), or appear in either report." Acceptance check: grant a full waiver and apply an advance on the same day; the day's Daily Collection Register total equals the cash and instruments physically handed over, and the period reconciliation difference is nil.

M17-13b [MUST] — application of an advance: "Applying an existing advance to an order shall be recorded as a row in the 'Applied to orders' child table of the originating advance Payment (M17.6), which shall carry a link to that Payment. It shall not create a new Payment record. The advance is counted as money received once, on the date it was tendered." Acceptance check: post one advance of Rs 10,000 and consume it across three orders; the customer ledger (M17-21) is correct at each step, exactly one Payment record exists, and the collection register shows the Rs 10,000 only on the day the advance was tendered.

M17-13c [MUST] — waiver: "An approved concession or waiver (M17-10) reduces the charge; it is never a receipt. Before the invoice is raised, it shall be applied at pricing and shall appear in the 'concession' column of M17-49. After the invoice is raised, the only instrument is a credit note under M17-35, referencing the waiver approval; the invoice-correction constraints of M17-36 apply unchanged. A waiver shall never reduce the amount shown as due on an issued tax invoice by a ledger entry alone." Acceptance check: grant a waiver before invoicing — the invoice is raised net and the concession column shows the amount; grant one after invoicing — the system requires a credit note and refuses a bare ledger adjustment.

Consequential edit: add "concession or waiver approved (M17-10)" to the M17-35 credit-note reason list, which currently offers only test not performed; sample rejected; sample insufficient; equipment unavailable; customer withdrew; over-charged; rate applied wrongly; other with text — with no waiver reason, removing Waiver from M17-13 would otherwise leave a post-invoice waiver with no recording route.

confirmed.problem: Giving the Administrator sight of every signatory's specimen signature image hands an IT role the means to produce a report that looks authorised without anyone authorising it, and it contradicts the M21.3 note that the Administrator "cannot authorise a report". Do not use the reviewer's wording. Replace M21-42 (parts\section_4_functional_support.md:1498) with:

"| M21-42 | [MUST] | Where a specimen **signature image** is printed, the stored image file shall be encrypted at rest as set out in NFR-52 and shall be readable by no user through any interface. It shall be visible only to the person it belongs to, and then only as a confirmation thumbnail on that person's own profile. No other user, **including the Administrator and the Quality Manager**, shall be able to view, download, export or apply it. This clause restricts the stored image asset; it does not restrict an issued report — an image rendered into a frozen report file under M8-43 forms part of that report and is printed, reprinted, downloaded and verified with it. | Attempt to open or download another person's signature image as the Administrator; refused and logged. Attempt to apply another person's signature image; refused and logged. Inspect the API response for a staff record and any staff-data export; the image bytes are not obtainable. Replace a person's image as the Administrator; the replacement succeeds, the old image is voided, and at no point is either image displayed. |"

Then amend M13-25's acceptance check (parts\section_4_functional_support.md:353) to: "Upload a specimen signature; it is visible only to the owner, cannot be viewed or downloaded by any other user including the Administrator, and cannot be exported." Keep M13-25's "as set out in M21" pointer, which is now correct.

M7-30 (parts\section_3_functional_core.md:1080) and ARC-45 (parts\section_5_nfr_plan.md:409) already state the correct rule and need no change — they are the anchor the edit aligns to. Confirm no new conflict is introduced: M8-40 already prints no signature on drafts, and M21-10 already logs print/export/download events, so the added retrieval log is consistent rather than duplicative.
confirmed.verifierReason:
VERIFIED VERBATIM. The quoted text exists exactly as given at D:\Prashant_WorkSpace\TTL Software\parts\section_4_functional_support.md:1498 (M21-42, assembled at SPEC.md:4423), and M13-25's acceptance check at the same file line 353 reads "it is visible only to the owner and the Administrator, and cannot be bulk-exported." Both cited locations and line numbers are accurate.

THE DEFECT IS REAL, AND IT IS PRIMARILY AN INTERNAL CONTRADICTION — which is stronger evidence than the reviewer's own framing. Three other [MUST] requirements state the tighter rule and exclude the Administrator:
- M7-30 (parts\section_3_functional_core.md:1080): "stored encrypted, accessible only to the owning user, never bulk-exportable, never applicable by another user"
- ARC-45 (parts\section_5_nfr_plan.md:409): "readable only by their owning user's action"
- NFR-52 (parts\section_5_nfr_plan.md:133): signature images "additionally encrypted at the file level with a key held outside the database"
So M21-42 and M13-25 are the two outliers, and M13-25 makes it worse by saying "stored with restricted access as set out in M21" — i.e. it defers to the looser clause as the governing definition. Two [MUST] requirements in direct conflict on an accreditation-critical control is not a matter of emphasis; an implementer reading M7-30 builds owner-only, one reading M21-42 builds owner-plus-admin.

The claimed conflict with the M21.3 note also checks out: parts\section_4_functional_support.md:1448 states the Administrator "cannot approve technical work, cannot authorise a report, and cannot alter the audit trail." Strictly, viewing an image does not grant the in-system authorise permission (M7-25/M21-41 still gate that), so this is not a formal logical contradiction — but it does hand the one role deliberately excluded from authorising the means to fabricate an out-of-band document that looks authorised, which is exactly the segregation the note is asserting.

An additional support the reviewer missed: the permission matrix (parts\section_4_functional_support.md:1414) grants the Administrator only **C** on "Staff master" — no **R**. The Quality Manager holds **R** there. So M21-42 grants read of the most sensitive field on that record to the one role the matrix gives no read at all, while withholding it from the role that does have read. M21-42 is inconsistent with the matrix in both directions.

RESEARCH CHECK. The source control is E4 at parts\research_nabl_17025.md:689: "access-restricted to the owning user, never bulk-exportable, never applied by another user, with a full usage log." No Administrator carve-out. M21-42 relaxes the researched control without stating a reason.

ONE REVIEWER OVERREACH, NOT MATERIAL. The reviewer says this "is the exact failure the research pack calls the most common finding on this topic." It is not. E4 attaches "the single most common finding on this topic" specifically to storing images "in an open shared folder," and ARC-45 repeats it that way. Administrator visibility is a weakening of E4, not the named most-common finding. This rhetorical inflation should be dropped from the finding text but does not defeat the substance.

THE PROPOSED FIX IS WRONG AND MUST NOT BE APPLIED AS DRAFTED. It is self-contradictory and it breaks the report pipeline:
1. Internally inconsistent: "shall be visible only to the person it belongs to" and "shall never return it to any screen, print preview or export" cannot both hold — the owner needs a screen to see it on.
2. It contradicts the premise of the very requirement it edits. M21-42 opens "Where a specimen signature image is printed". The image's whole purpose is to be rendered onto the issued report. M8-43 (parts\section_3_functional_core.md:1242) freezes the issued report as bytes and requires that it be served for "display, download, reprint or verification"; M8-65 (line 1274) covers reprints; the customer portal downloads it. Forbidding the image from any "print preview or export" outlaws the issued report itself. (M8-40, line 1232, already correctly excludes signatures from watermarked drafts, so drafts are not the problem — issued reports are.)
3. Deleting "and the Administrator" from M13-25 leaves that clause pointing at M21 for its definition, so the fix must land in M21-42 or M13-25 silently re-inherits the loose rule.
4. It creates an operational dead end the spec needs an answer for: no one can load or replace an image for a new joiner or a corrupted file.
The corrected fix below separates the two things the reviewer conflated — the stored image asset (which no one should be able to read) from the image already rendered inside a frozen signed report (which is legitimately printed and downloaded) — and adds upload/replace-without-read for the Administrator.

confirmed.location: section_5_nfr_plan.md DB-08 (line 550) vs section_2_workflow.md WF-97 (line 771), WF-99 (line 773), DB-10 (line 552), AC-31 (line 880)
confirmed.quote: Allocation runs in **its own short transaction**: lock the single counter row (`SELECT last_number FROM mst_numbering_counter WHERE ... FOR UPDATE`), increment it, commit. The number is then used in the business transaction.

Its amended AC-31 also deletes the failed-transaction void-register clause, leaving DB-10 and the sys_number_void table with no stated path for a consumed number and weakening a General Financial Rules justification the spec explicitly invokes. It also does not check DB-13 (ULR allotted at report authorisation) or NFR-18 (batch allocation of 30 sample numbers in one action), both of which allocate through "the same mechanism as DB-08".

That is the genuinely missing piece, and it should be fixed by adding the recovery duty, not by discarding DB-08.

(2) NFR-97 (line 228) — "Backup schedule: a full database backup every night; transaction logs every 15 minutes; **issued controlled-document files (report PDFs, signed invoices, receipts, credit notes) are copied to the local backup disk as part of the business action that issues them, and the issue is not confirmed until that copy exists and its SHA-256 matches the stored fingerprint — this copy is to a local disk only, never a synchronous off-site upload, so that §24.1's rule and NFR-16's 5-second budget still hold**; all other attachments backed up nightly (changed files only); a monthly full backup retained for 12 months; a yearly full backup retained for 7 years."

(3) NFR-98 (line 229) — first copy becomes "one on a **third, separate, non-mirrored internal disk dedicated to backups** (the mirror in NFR-116 is a single logical volume and therefore is not a second copy)".

Three requirements then close the trap: DB-01 (line 543) puts `created_by_user_id BIGINT NOT NULL` on **every** table; DB-05 refuses any write with no session user; NFR-47 (line 128) demands "Zero shared accounts.
