rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
The quote is genuine (D:\Prashant_WorkSpace\TTL Software\parts\section_3_functional_core.md:1216, M8-33), but both halves of the finding fail on the document.

1. "Unreachable at go-live / weeks of day-one cost" is a misreading — the spec already defers exactly this apparatus, and to a LATER phase than the reviewer proposes. D:\Prashant_WorkSpace\TTL Software\parts\section_5_nfr_plan.md:679 (§26.6, "Phase 4 — The quality system (5 weeks)") lists as Included: "the Unique Laboratory Report number configuration engine, the accredited-scope master, the in-scope flag per test and the automatic split of a mixed order into an accredited report and a non-accredited report". Phase 1's Included list (§26.3, line 641) contains report generation with the frozen PDF, fingerprint, QR and internal signature — and no ULR, no scope master, no symbol, no split. Priority tags ([MUST]/[SHOULD]) are per-requirement importance in this document; delivery sequencing lives in §26. The finding assumes [MUST] == day one, which the document never says.

2. The gate the reviewer asks for already exists. §26.2 PLN-06 (line 626) requires obtaining "the accreditation position of the unit" in writing during Phase 0 — before any of this is coded. The "not accredited by default" rule is stated four times independently: OPEN-Q6 (section_3:1221), OPEN-Q12 (section_2:794), OPEN-Q8 (section_4:408), OPEN-Q-B12/C6/D8 in appendix.md, and in front_matter.md:48 ("The system defaults to not accredited and prints no claim until a certificate is produced"). The reviewer's Phase 1 rule — no symbol and no ULR unless every parameter is flagged Yes — is already M8-31 (hard block) plus M8-40 (a draft prints neither) plus those defaults.

3. The proposed fix would make things worse. Tagging items "[LATER — Phase 2]" collides with the spec's own defined vocabulary, where Phase 2 = "Money and statutory returns (6 weeks)" (§26.4); it would pull accreditation work forward from Phase 4 into the billing phase. The fix is also internally inconsistent: it retags M8-30 to Phase 2 while Phase 1 is said to keep the per-test in_accredited_scope boolean, which is M8-30; and it retags M8-27 (the ULR requirement) while keeping a Phase 1 rule governing when a ULR may print. M8-36 is misclassified as accreditation machinery — it is a [SHOULD] template layout option for printing discipline and group, which the research brief calls "harmless and cheap to print" (research_nabl_17025.md:780).

4. M8-33 is not unmoored. It traces verbatim to research requirement N7 (research_nabl_17025.md:110: "Forbid asterisks/footnote markers ... Lint the template at build time; block any `*`-based 'not in NABL scope' annotation pattern"), which rests on directly quoted, dated, cited sources — NABL 133 cl. 5.1 (Issue 09, Amd. 03, 03-Sep-2024) and cl. 6.2, both quoted at research_nabl_17025.md:92-95 — i.e. [F]-grade, not overstated. It is named as the #2 pitfall at research_nabl_17025.md:725. The acceptance check pins the canonical case concretely ("Add an asterisk-based 'not in scope' note ... the build fails"), and templates are not free prose (M8-26 forces statements to be referenced by code), so the "units footnote false positive" is speculative. The reviewer's replacement text also duplicates M8-34, which already requires the review-checklist item and the Quality Manager's template sign-off — so the fix deletes a cheap CI regex and substitutes a control that is already specified.

Residual worth at most a Minor wording nit, not the finding as filed: M8-33's phrase "any pattern that marks a parameter as outside scope with a symbol" is open-ended for a static check. If anything is done, tighten it in place rather than delete it — e.g. "The accredited template must not contain asterisk, dagger or other footnote-marker glyphs against a parameter row or in a note that distinguishes accreditation status. A build-time template lint rejects these glyphs in the accredited template" — leaving M8-34's sign-off as the human backstop. One genuine (trivial) day-one item does exist and is deliberate: M1-68 requires a configured numbering series for the ULR before go-live, and OPEN-Q-B12's default keeps that series switched off. That is one disabled master row, not weeks.

rejectedForTheRecord.location: M21, M21-11 (line 1452) and the note under the M21.3 matrix (line 1448)
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: The Administrator can edit the role-permission mapping and holds C,U on "Role and permission changes". Nothing stops the Administrator granting the Administrator role "Report — authorise and issue", "Result — verify", "Impact analysis — disposition" or "Audit trail — edit or delete", acting, and reverting. The note's claim that the Administrator "cannot approve technical work, cannot authorise a report, and cannot alter the audit trail" is therefore false as specified — it describes the current data, not a control. The matrix shows AA as "A" on that row but no requirement makes that approval a precondition. This is a self-escalation path and an assessor who tests it will find it.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
The quote is genuine (SPEC.md:4377, parts/section_4_functional_support.md:1452) and the note is genuine (SPEC.md:4373). But every load-bearing claim in the finding is falsified by requirements outside M21.3.

1. "No requirement makes AA approval a precondition" — false. M21-58 [MUST] (SPEC.md:4449): "A change shall not go live without an authorisation and a test-evidence record. This applies to configuration changes as much as to program changes — a change to a calculation formula, a decision rule, a rate, a report template or **a permission** is a validated change." M21-57 (4448) makes "permission change" an explicit change-control category recording "who requested, who authorised", complete "before the change goes live". The precondition the reviewer asks for already exists.

2. "Nothing stops the Administrator granting itself 'Report — authorise and issue' / 'Result — verify'" — false. The permission matrix is only the function-level layer. Authorisation to act is a separate, separately-owned register: M13-07 holds one row per (person, method version, activity) with activities including TECHNICAL_REVIEW and AUTHORISE_REPORT (M13.4, SPEC.md:3302-3313); M13-08 [MUST] "The matrix shall be enforced, not merely displayed" refuses, at the moment of the action, "technically reviewing a result; authorising or signing a report" by an unauthorised person. M13-11 holds the Authorised Signatory Register "**distinct from the general matrix**"; M13-12, M7-25, M7-35 and M21-41 all re-verify signatory scope for every test on the report at the moment of signing. In the matrix itself the Administrator has "–" on "Competency authorisation" (SPEC.md:4340) — creation is LI, approval is AA. Granting AD the M21.3 permission yields the screen, not the act. Regression tests 3, 4 and 5 (SPEC.md:4478-4480) are mandated negative tests for exactly this.

3. "Administrator could grant itself 'Audit trail — edit or delete'" — false, and this is the clearest error. M21-31 [MUST]: "no user, no role, and specifically **not the Administrator**, shall be able to edit or delete an audit entry. Update and delete rights on the audit tables shall be revoked from the application's database account", with M21-26 requiring database-level (trigger) capture. Regression test 8: "Edit an audit entry as the Administrator | Refused". No matrix edit can reach this.

4. "Hard-code that delete is never grantable" — already there: matrix legend "**D** delete (never granted anywhere)", M21-33 soft-delete-only, M13-26, and regression test 7 "No delete exists; **database refuses**".

So the note is not "false as specified": each of its three assertions rests on a control outside the configurable matrix, not on the current data. The reviewer read M21.3 and M21-11 in isolation and did not check M13, M21.7-M21.10 or M7.

Residual point, genuinely not stated but minor: nothing explicitly forbids the circular move of the Administrator granting the Administrator role the "A" mark on "Role and permission changes" and then self-authorising, since M21-58 requires "an authorisation" without naming the authoriser as a different person. That would be worth one clarifying clause on M21-11 ("the authorisation required by M21-58 for a permission change shall be given by the Approving Authority and shall not be given by the user who requested the change"), but it is a Minor drafting hardening, not a Blocker, and it does not produce the consequences claimed — report authorisation, result verification and audit tampering remain blocked by M13-08/M13-12/M21-41 and M21-31 regardless.

The proposed fix would also introduce contradictions. Hard-coding "report authorisation for any role other than Approving Authority" collides with M13-13/M13-14 (Delegation Register — time-bounded delegation of authorisation to another person), M13-11's "designated alternate" and M7-35's no-signatory-available rule; the spec deliberately delegates at person level, not role level. "Delete on any record" and audit-trail immutability duplicate M21-33/M21-31 and would create two differently-worded statements of the same control. "Disabling of audit capture" prohibits a capability the specification never offers (no such switch exists in M21.11).

rejectedForTheRecord.location: M22.1 ownership table, rows "Service classification code and tax code per service" (line 1706) and "Tax masters and rates" (line 1715), against M17-30 (line 875) and M17-31 (line 876)
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: M22 opens with "for every field, exactly one system is the master" and then breaks its own rule. M17-30 makes the LIMS master of a dated tax master ("never written into program code"), M17-31 makes the LIMS master of the classification code per rate card line, and M21.11 lists `tax_rate_master` as a LIMS configuration switch — while M22.1 assigns both to CloudZoo ERP. The developer has to pick, and picking wrong produces two systems computing different tax on the same invoice. Worse, it assumes CloudZoo holds a dated tax master and a per-service SAC code — exactly the kind of ERP capability the section elsewhere says it cannot know exists — and this assumption is absent from the M22.3 assumption list.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
The quotes are verbatim (SPEC.md lines 4631, 4640), but the premise is a misreading of M17. M17's own opening ownership paragraph (SPEC.md line 3735) states: "CloudZoo ERP should own the accounting ledger - the tax invoice..., the credit note, THE TAX MASTERS, and the general ledger. The LIMS should own the commercial decision... Full table in M22." M22.1's two rows are the elaboration of a decision M17 states itself and explicitly delegates to M22. No contradiction exists.

M17-30 and M17-31 never assign mastership. M17-30 requires the rate be "held in a dated tax master, never written into program code" - a prohibition on hard-coding, fully satisfied by M22.1's "read-only copy with effective dates." M17-31 is a granularity rule ("per rate card line, not once for the whole invoice"), with an acceptance check about a testing line and a machine-rental line each carrying their own code. M1-60 (line 1389) defines the LIMS Tax master entity (tax code, SAC/HSN, CGST/SGST/IGST percentages, treatment, effective dates) and M1-53 gives the rate card line a `tax code` field that references it - so the LIMS masters WHICH code applies to which line ("rate application"), while the ERP masters the code and rate VALUES. That is precisely M22.1's split, and M22's governing rule ("exactly one system is the master, the other holds a read-only copy") is honoured, not broken.

The "assumption absent from M22.3" claim is false. The document names ERP tax-code ownership as a Blocking open question twice: OPEN-Q-T8 (line 5636, marked Blocking) - "Which fields does CloudZoo own... Specifically: customer master, tax registration, invoice, receipt, TAX CODES, asset register..." with recommended default "CloudZoo owns customer identity, invoice, receipt, TAX and asset value. The laboratory system owns... RATE APPLICATION..."; and OPEN-Q-T7 (line 5635, Blocking) - "CloudZoo as the system of record for customer identity, tax registration, invoices, receipts and assets."

The M21.11 evidence does not support the finding either: that table's heading (line 4501) is "Configuration and feature switches introduced by this document" - a defaults catalogue, not a mastership statement. `tax_rate_master` default "Empty until confirmed in writing" tracks OPEN-Q-D19 ("print nothing until that confirmation exists"), which holds whichever system supplies the figure; and M22-17 requires the LIMS to run with the integration switched off entirely, so local holding of the values is required regardless of mastership.

The claimed failure mode is also not reachable as described: M22.1's Tax invoice row is "LIMS -> ERP to create", so the LIMS computes and prints the tax from its dated copy and the ERP posts what it is sent; the stale-copy case is explicitly handled in the row's own failure-handling column ("LIMS uses the last known dated rate and flags any invoice raised while out of sync").

The proposed fix would introduce three NEW contradictions the reviewer did not check: it contradicts M17's line 3735 ownership preamble, the recommended default of OPEN-Q-T8 (Blocking), and OPEN-Q-T7 (Blocking). The "Rate card / price list" reword is also unnecessary - that row's Direction column already reads "LIMS -> ERP as the invoice line amount", which pins the ERP's "posted price" to the amount it was sent, consistent with M17-06's price snapshot and M1-55's historical reprints. The only residual is that M22.3's eight assumptions do not restate the ERP tax-master assumption locally, which is a marginal editorial nicety already covered by two Blocking open questions - not a Blocker contradiction, and not enough to rescue a finding built on a misreading.

rejectedForTheRecord.location: M15-27 (line 627) against M13-08 (line 336), M13.5 rule 6 (line 402), M20-35 (line 1220) and M21.10 test 3 (line 1553)
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: M13-08 refuses unauthorised action outright and logs the refusal; M13.5 rule 6 says explicitly "the entry is refused and a Nonconformity is the correct outcome, not an override"; regression test 3 expects "Refused" with no override clause, unlike test 4 which does have one. Yet M15-27 and M20-35 both describe an unauthorised-person override as an existing feature. A developer reading M15 will build the override, and a laboratory told it has one will use it — a straight 6.2.6 failure, and precisely the gate the reader was told is "the difference between a compliant laboratory and a laboratory with a filing cabinet".
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
The quote is real (M15-27, parts/section_4_functional_support.md:627), but the finding's central premise — that an unauthorised-person override is described as an existing feature ONLY in M15-27 and M20-35 while the rest of the document refuses outright — is factually wrong. The override is independently specified in three other places the reviewer did not consult:

1. M5-06 [MUST] (parts/section_3_functional_core.md:714): "Both the competency gate and the calibration gate may be overridden only by the Unit Incharge, only with a reason from the override reason list, and the override automatically opens a nonconformity record. Every refused attempt is also logged."
2. DB-32 (parts/section_5_nfr_plan.md:581): "An observation cannot be recorded by a person without a valid authorisation for that method and the 'perform' activity on observed_at. Trigger against mst_competency; same override pattern." — i.e. the DB-30/DB-31 pattern of authorised user + reason + raises a nonconformity.
3. AC-14 (parts/section_5_nfr_plan.md:848), an acceptance criterion covering exactly the "tester attempts to enter a result directly" case: "both refusals are logged; the override, if used, requires an authorised person, a reason, and opens a nonconforming work record."

So M15-27 and M20-35 are consistent with the specification; there is nothing for a developer to invent.

The two texts the reviewer reads as prohibitions do not prohibit. M13-08 mandates the block and the logging of every refusal; it nowhere states the block is unoverridable. M13.5 rule 6 is explicitly scoped to retrospective data entry, where the person was unauthorised on the observation date and competence cannot be retro-fitted — a genuinely different case from the forward-looking, Unit-Incharge-authorised, nonconformity-raising override of M5-06. Two different things that legitimately differ.

The test-3-versus-test-4 asymmetry argument also fails: M21.10 tests 1 and 2 (out-of-calibration instrument, expired consumable batch) are likewise bare "Refused", yet M6-14, M6-15, DB-30 and DB-31 unambiguously grant overrides for both, and M15-27 lists both as override-triggered nonconformities. The missing "unless overridden" clause is a uniform convention across tests 1-3, not evidence that no override exists for unauthorised persons.

The research brief does not support the claim either. parts/research_nabl_17025.md:393 and :731 record 6.2.6 as requiring a per-activity authorisation matrix, and name the actual failure mode as "Role-based access only, with no per-method analyst authorisation" — which the specification implements. No brief line says a logged, supervisor-authorised departure is a 6.2.6 breach.

Finally, the proposed fix would introduce three new contradictions and weaken compliance. Rewriting M15-27 to trigger on "work nonetheless performed by another route" makes the trigger contingent on an event the system by definition cannot detect, and destroys the automatic nonconformity that M5-06, DB-32 and AC-14 all require for the override itself. Deleting "unauthorised person" from M20-35 removes exactly the management-review visibility M5-06 exists to produce. And the sentence "There shall be no override of this refusal. No role, including the Approving Authority, may grant a competency exemption at the point of action" contradicts M5-06 [MUST], DB-32 and AC-14 head-on, converting a logged, nonconformity-raising departure into an undocumented one — worse under 6.2.6, not better.

The only residual point is editorial and Minor, and it is not what the finding asks for: M13-08 and M13.5 rule 6 would read more clearly with a cross-reference to M5-06's override, and M21.10 tests 1-3 could carry the "unless overridden, and the override raises a nonconformity" clause that tests 4 and 12 already use.

rejectedForTheRecord.location: M11-14 (line 41) against M11-36 (line 63) and the M21.3 matrix row "Calibration event — record" (line 1400)
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: This is tagged [SHOULD], so the developer may legitimately ship without it, while M11-36 [MUST] says corrections in this module are made only by voiding, and the matrix grants the Lab In-Charge "U" on calibration events. An editable correction factor silently rewrites every result computed inside that calibration's validity window (M11-13 feeds it to the calculation engine), with no impact analysis and nothing on the report to say the number changed. That is a 6.4.11 and 7.5.2 failure, and it is the one edit in the whole module that changes reported values retroactively.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
The finding is a misreading built on a truncated quote, and its central harm claim is contradicted by a [MUST] requirement elsewhere in the document.

(1) TRUNCATED QUOTE. parts/section_4_functional_support.md:41 actually reads: "The system shall prevent a user from editing a stored correction factor. Corrections are made by voiding the calibration event (with reason) and recording a replacement." with acceptance check "Attempt to edit a correction factor; the field is read-only and the screen offers 'Void and re-record'." The reviewer cut the requirement at the first period, dropping both the void-and-replace mechanism and the acceptance check, then proposed re-adding them as if they were missing.

(2) THE HARM MECHANISM IS ALREADY PREVENTED AT [MUST]. The claim that an editable correction factor "silently rewrites every result computed inside that calibration's validity window" is false against this spec. parts/section_3_functional_core.md:884, M6-16 [MUST]: "Where the calibration certificate carries a correction factor, the current factor is applied automatically by the calculation engine, ITS VALUE IS STORED ON THE RESULT, and the factor's version is recorded. Applying a stale factor must be impossible." Acceptance check: "Update a balance's correction factor; new results use the new factor and OLD RESULTS RETAIN THE OLD ONE." Reinforced by the result field table at parts/section_3_functional_core.md:960: "Correction factor applied | Derived | Auto | From the current calibration record | Read-only; version stored." Results carry a snapshot of the applied value and its version, so no edit to the master factor can retroactively change a computed result. There is no retroactive rewrite to be had.

(3) THE 7.5.2 CLAIM FAILS. Everything 7.5.2 demands is carried at [MUST] in M21.5 (parts/section_4_functional_support.md:1477-1484): M21-27 records old value, new value, actor, timestamp and reason for change; M21-28 [MUST] explicitly NAMES "a calibration record" among the records for which "a reason for change is mandatory and cannot be blank"; M21-29 [MUST] "The original value shall remain visible in the interface" with a change marker and view-history; M21-30 [MUST] a printed technical record shows the original alongside the amendment; M21-31 makes the audit trail immutable even to the Administrator; M21-33 [MUST] soft-delete/void only. The reviewer's "nothing on the report to say the number changed" is directly answered by M21-29 and M21-30.

(4) THE 6.4.11 CLAIM FAILS, AND THE MATRIX "U" IS THE RESEARCH BRIEF'S OWN RECOMMENDED CONTROL. parts/research_nabl_17025.md:318 maps clause 6.4.11 to "Correction factors are versioned data attached to the calibration certificate, automatically applied by the calculation engine and available at the point of use" — that is exactly M11-13 [MUST] ("dated, versioned data attached to that calibration event... available to the calculation engine for results observed within that calibration's validity period"). Line 319 maps the adjacent clause 6.4.12 to "restrict who may change instrument configuration/correction factors; LOG EVERY CHANGE" — i.e. restricted-plus-logged change, not absolute immutability. LI-only "U" (parts/section_4_functional_support.md:1400) plus the M21 audit trail IS that control. The matrix row is not a compliance defect.

(5) TWO MORE PRE-EXISTING BACKSTOPS. M7-12(e) [MUST] makes "the correction factor applied was the current one" a mandatory verification checklist item; M7-14 [MUST] re-executes every calculation from stored raw readings and "A difference blocks verification and raises a nonconformity."

(6) THE [SHOULD] PREMISE IS MISSTATED. parts/section_1_foundation.md:5 defines [SHOULD] as "it is needed but can follow shortly" — not "may legitimately ship without it." More importantly, M11-36 [MUST] itself states "Corrections are made by voiding with a reason" for calibration events, so the no-edit rule is already carried at MUST level. M11-14 is a redundant restatement of the enforcement mechanism, not a licence to ship an editable field. The reviewer inverts this: the alleged "contradiction" is in fact the MUST-level requirement already covering the case.

(7) THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD INTRODUCE NEW CONTRADICTIONS. (a) "No field of a saved calibration event — ... valid-from, valid-until — shall be editable after save" directly contradicts the M11.6 field table at parts/section_4_functional_support.md:122: "Valid until / next due | Date | Yes | Default = valid from + interval, editable with reason". (b) Freezing every field contradicts M11-09 [MUST], whose "Certificate missing" warning presumes a certificate can be attached to an already-saved event later; the fix would force a full void-and-re-record for a clerical omission. (c) "Remove 'U' from the LI column ... leaving C for SK and A for LI/AA" is factually wrong about the row, which is LI=U, AA=A, QM=R, SK=C; the fix would ADD approve authority to the Lab In-Charge that the row does not currently grant, expanding the authority model well beyond anything the finding argues for, and would leave no role able to correct a calibration event at all despite M21-28 [MUST] contemplating exactly such reasoned changes.

RESIDUAL SLIVER (not the finding as filed, and far below Blocker): M11-24's trigger list (calibration fails / intermediate check fails / fault reported / calibration discovered lapsed) does not include "voiding a calibration event whose correction factors have already been applied," so auto-opening Impact Analysis on that specific path is unspecified. That is a Minor enhancement to M11-24's trigger enumeration, not a 6.4.11/7.5.2 compliance failure, because M6-16, M7-12(e), M7-14, M21-27/28/29/30 already make any such change non-retroactive, reasoned, traceable, visible on the printed record and detectable at verification.

rejectedForTheRecord.location: M13-13 (line 341), M13-14 (line 342), against M13-11 (line 339) and M21-41 (line 1497)
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: This is the only constraint on delegation and it is the wrong one. A Unit In-Charge who holds AUTHORISE_REPORT can delegate it for five days to a Technical Assistant who is not in the Authorised Signatory Register at all. M21-41 then checks that "the signer holds a valid authorisation" — which the delegation has just created — so the check passes and a report goes out signed by a person never declared as responsible for reviewing, reporting and authorising results. That is a direct NABL 133 cl. 6.3 failure and it is the report-signing hole an assessor looks for first.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
The quote is genuine (D:\Prashant_WorkSpace\TTL Software\SPEC.md:3267 = parts\section_4_functional_support.md:342), but the load-bearing claim — "This is the only constraint on delegation and it is the wrong one" — is false. The reviewer only read M13 and missed that delegation is specified primarily in M7, under its own heading "Delegation — because it will happen" (SPEC.md:2329-2335, authored at parts\section_3_functional_core.md:1086).

The exact rule the reviewer says is absent is already there, twice:

1. M7-31 [MUST] (SPEC.md:2331): "The delegate must independently hold a valid authorisation for that scope; delegation cannot create competence." Acceptance check: "Delegate to a person without the underlying authorisation; blocked. Delegate to an authorised alternate; permitted for the stated dates only."
2. M7 rules and edge cases, item 7 (SPEC.md:2387): "Delegation does not create competence. The alternate must already hold the authorisation. Delegation only transfers the act of signing, for a bounded period, with a record."

The proposed fix's core sentence — "Delegation shall never create signatory authority the delegate does not independently hold" — is therefore a near-verbatim restatement of existing text.

The specific scenario is independently blocked three more times:
- M7-25 [MUST] (SPEC.md:2320) is unconditional: "Authorisation is performed only by a person on the laboratory's Authorised Signatory register, and only for the specific disciplines... The system verifies coverage for every parameter on the report and refuses otherwise." A Technical Assistant not in the register cannot sign, delegation or not.
- M7-35 [MUST] (SPEC.md:2335): where no signatory is available and no valid delegation exists the report is held — "Work waits; it is not signed by an unauthorised person."
- M13-12 [MUST] (SPEC.md:3265): the authorisation step verifies "the signatory is authorised for every test appearing on that report, not merely that they are a signatory."

So M21-41's check is not satisfied by a self-created authorisation: M7-31 prevents the delegation from existing in the first place, and M7-25 gates the signing act on independent register membership. The alleged NABL 133 cl. 6.3 failure does not arise. The register itself carries the declaration reference to the accreditation body and a designated alternate (M13-11, M7-26), the data model backs it (mst_personnel: is_authorised_signatory, declared_to_nabl_on, alternate_personnel_id, SPEC.md:5172), and signatory changes raise a 15-day notification task (M7-34, M13-19). M7-33 also forces the report to print the delegate's own name, never the absent person's.

The second half of the proposed fix would introduce a new contradiction. Requiring that signing rest on "the signer's own Authorised Signatory entry — not a delegation" contradicts M7-31, M7-33 and M7-35, which deliberately permit a register-listed alternate to sign under a recorded, time-bounded, printed delegation while the primary signatory is on tour — a case the document raises explicitly in its opening rationale (SPEC.md:17) and in OPEN-Q-A6 (SPEC.md:265).

The only residual point is editorial and trivial: M13-14 does not cross-reference M7-31, so read in isolation M13's phrase "an activity the delegating authority does not itself hold" constrains the delegator's scope rather than restating the delegate-side test. Adding "see M7-31" to M13-14 would help a reader, but that is a cross-reference nit, not a Major compliance risk, and nothing in the specification permits the hole described.

rejectedForTheRecord.location: M12-22 (line 211); whole of M11, M12 and M15
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: Two gaps, both assessable. First, the only external-provider control in these modules is [SHOULD], warn-only, and scoped to goods suppliers — yet the providers whose competence actually underpins the results are calibration laboratories (M11-08 and M11-10 rely on their accredited scope), proficiency-testing providers (M15-11) and sister CSB units doing inter-laboratory comparisons (M15-14). None is subject to evaluation, approval or lapse-checking anywhere. Second, M17-09 explicitly supports work "received here, tested at another unit" — the laboratory subcontracts — and there is no subcontracted-test register, no customer-approval-before-sending gate, and no per-parameter flag forcing externally provided results to be identified on the report. Clause 6.6.3 and 7.1.1(c) are not implemented anywhere in M11-M22.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
The quote is genuine (D:\Prashant_WorkSpace\TTL Software\parts\section_4_functional_support.md line 211 = SPEC.md line 3136), but both halves of the claimed gap collapse against the document.

SECOND GAP IS FACTUALLY WRONG. The reviewer asserts "there is no subcontracted-test register, no customer-approval-before-sending gate, and no per-parameter flag forcing externally provided results to be identified on the report" and that "7.1.1(c) [is] not implemented anywhere". All three exist as [MUST] requirements with acceptance checks, outside M11-M22:
- SPEC.md:1052 (parts\section_2_workflow.md:610) — Allocation state **Subcontracted**: "Requires a recorded customer notification and the customer's approval before the state may be entered. Records the external laboratory and, where relevant, its accreditation reference. Flags the allocation so the report identifies the external provider." The allocation is the per-parameter object, so this *is* the per-parameter register and flag.
- SPEC.md:1134 WF-83 [MUST] — refusal gate with acceptance check "Attempt to subcontract without the approval record. Refused. After subcontracting, the issued report names the external provider against that parameter."
- SPEC.md:2439 M8-16 [MUST] and SPEC.md:2542 report field "External provider per line"; SPEC.md:2426 M8-03 [MUST] location of testing per line.
- Upstream consent: SPEC.md:1569 and :1701 "Must become Yes/Granted before any referral"; M3-09 (:1629); M2-17 carries subcontracting approvals forward; M1-34 (:1333) flags referred tests and "prompts for the subcontracting workflow in M3"; M4-22 custody events include "Transferred to subcontractor".
- Data model already carries it: SPEC.md:5194 `txn_order_line.subcontract_to`, `subcontract_customer_approved_at`.
M17-09 is a billing requirement (receiving/testing/billing unit on the statutory return); the technical control lives in the workflow module by design. Module-scoped absence is not a defect when the capability is deliberately placed elsewhere and cross-referenced.

FIRST GAP IS LARGELY A MISREADING. (a) M12-22 is not "scoped to goods suppliers" — it reads "items **or categories** approved for", and M21-82 [MUST] (section_4:1679) already places a pure *service* provider (the hosting/maintenance party) on the same approved supplier list "with periodic re-evaluation", so the list is the general external-provider register. (b) Calibration providers are controlled harder than an ASL entry: M11-08 [MUST] (SPEC.md:2960) refuses save without the calibrating agency's accreditation certificate number **and the specific accredited scope line relied on**; the M11.6 field table (section_4:106-108) makes "Agency accreditation valid until" mandatory and warns if expired at date performed — that is the lapse check the reviewer says exists nowhere; M11-10 requires written justification for a non-accredited (Tier 3) provider; M11-11 prints the chain with accreditation number and validity. (c) M15-11 [MUST] records "whether the provider is accredited for proficiency testing". Research brief research_nabl_17025.md:363-365 maps 6.6.3 precisely to the Approved Supplier List the spec implements, and Q5 (:468) to the PT register the spec implements.

THE FIX WOULD CREATE CONTRADICTIONS. Hard-refusing any calibration booking against a provider without a valid accreditation certificate collides head-on with M11-10, which deliberately permits Tier 1 (National Metrology Institute — NPL India is not NABL-accredited) and Tier 3 (17025-compliant but not accredited for that line, with justification); mandating "accreditation certificate number ... and validity date" for every calibration and subcontract lab also contradicts the spec's deliberate "where relevant, its accreditation reference" for sister CSB units, which are frequently unaccredited. Hard-blocking indents contradicts the M12.4 batch field "Supplier | Link to Approved Supplier List **or text**" (section_4:248) and the M22 mapping row (:1721) where the ERP may hold the vendor master. And proposed M12-33 puts a subcontracted-test register in the consumables/stock module, duplicating WF-83/M8-16 and splitting one rule across two homes, with a release-time gate that is weaker than the existing send-time refusal.

Residual sliver only: no 6.6.3(b)-style evaluation/score/re-evaluation-date record for service providers specifically (calibration, PT, ILC), and no explicit requirement to attach the external laboratory's report file to a Subcontracted allocation. That is editorial/Minor at most, not a Major missing capability, and nothing like the rewrite proposed.

rejectedForTheRecord.problem: "Run" is the pivot of the entire quality-control gate — it decides which customer reports are withheld when a control fails — and it is never defined, never a field in any field table, and never stored on anything. A developer cannot implement it, and two developers would implement it differently (all tests that day? all tests on that instrument? all tests in one tray?). Too narrow and a failed control withholds nothing; too wide and one failed control freezes the laboratory. This is the most important undefined term in M15.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected: The finding rests on three factual claims that are all false against the document. (a) "Never defined": the unit of work is defined, under the document's deliberately renamed term **Worksheet** — glossary at SPEC.md:389 ("A run sheet grouping many tests together for one person's session at the bench, including any quality-control positions"), and normatively in M5-13 [MUST] at SPEC.md:1971 ("a worksheet groups allocations that are physically run together in one session, across many samples and many customers, on one instrument, by one tester, under one method"), with its stored fields listed in M5-14 (worksheet number, date, section, analyst, instrument, method revision, atmosphere at start and end of the run, state) and its QC positions in M5-15 (blank, duplicate, reference material, blind/spiked control). (b) "Never a field in any field table": it is a field in at least two — the M5 Allocate/Reallocate field table at SPEC.md:2060 ("| Worksheet | Lookup or 'create new' | No | Same method revision, same instrument, same tester | Groups the run |") and the M6 result-entry field table (parts/section_3_functional_core.md:957, "Same method, tester and instrument"). (c) "Never stored on anything": the settled-vocabulary table at SPEC.md:965 assigns it the database table `txn_worksheet` ("Batch run sheet | Worksheet | txn_worksheet"), M5-07 requires the allocation to record "the worksheet if any", and M1-68 gives Worksheet its own numbering series. The research brief confirms the intended mapping and even the schema (parts/research_lims_reference.md:52 "Worksheet / batch / run sheet — Group many tests across many samples into one run, with QC positions"; :261 `txn_worksheet_line` with `line_type` sample/blank/duplicate/reference/spike). Separately, the withhold scope is pinned in context and not left to the developer: M15-02 [MUST] requires the control result to be "linked to the analyst, the instrument, the consumable batch, the environmental record and the customer samples in the same run", with the acceptance check "Record a control; the linked customer tests are listed on the control record" — so M15-04 acts on an explicitly recorded link set, defeating the claimed "all tests that day? all tests on that instrument?" ambiguity. The proposed fix is also wrong: it invents a parallel "Run" entity duplicating `txn_worksheet`, which breaches WF-23 (the 8.3 words must be used identically in UI, tables and columns) and section 8.4's prohibition on alternative names for the worksheet; a mandatory run identifier on every observation contradicts M5-07 ("the worksheet if any") and the "Mandatory? No" worksheet fields; and "closes at end of day" would split legitimately overnight sessions (24 h pre-conditioning, oven drying runs recorded start-and-end per M16-20). The only real residual is cosmetic — M15 writes "run" where the settled word is "Worksheet", and does not name the fallback for an allocation with no worksheet — a Minor wording/terminology nit, far from "the most important undefined term in M15".

rejectedForTheRecord.location: M17-29 (line 874), M17-27 (line 872), M17.6 field table (lines 904-921)
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: The intent is right, but "place of supply state" is never a stored field, never appears in a field table, and no rule is given for deriving it. The invoice field list requires it to be printed; nothing says where it comes from. So the developer will do the one thing the requirement forbids — put a state dropdown on the invoice screen. For a laboratory whose customers are traders and exporters across state lines, and whose own registration state is itself unconfirmed (OPEN-Q18), this is the field the entire tax split turns on.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
The quote is genuine (D:\Prashant_WorkSpace\TTL Software\parts\section_4_functional_support.md line 874 = SPEC.md line 3799), but the two load-bearing factual claims behind it are false.

1. "Never a stored field, never appears in a field table" — FALSE. The data dictionary carries it explicitly. SPEC.md line 5208 (parts\section_5_nfr_plan.md line 492), `txn_invoice`: `gst_registration_id`, `customer_id`, `place_of_supply_state_code CHAR(2)`, `is_interstate BOOLEAN`, `reverse_charge BOOLEAN`, `cgst`, `sgst`, `igst`. Both sides of the comparison M17-29 demands are stored: the supplier side in `mst_gst_registration` (`state_code CHAR(2)`, `effective_from/to`, SPEC.md line 5144) linked from `mst_unit.gst_registration_id` (line 5143), and the recipient side as `place_of_supply_state_code` on the invoice, with the outcome cached in `is_interstate`. The reviewer's cited "M17.6 field table (lines 904-921)" is the **Payment** field table — place of supply would not belong there. M17 has no invoice field table at all, which is a different (and much weaker) observation than the one made.

2. "No rule is given for deriving it" — the derivation inputs and their purpose are stated in the customer master field table (SPEC.md lines 1446, 1453): "Is registered business entity for tax | Yes / No | Yes | Default No | **Drives place-of-supply logic**" and "State | Pick-list | Yes | Indian states and union territories with codes | **Drives tax split**". GSTIN validation at line 1447 additionally forces "state code must match address state", closing the gap between the registered-recipient branch and the address branch. That is the s.12(2) IGST Act two-branch rule (registered → recipient's location; unregistered → address on record) expressed through the field notes rather than as prose — and the research brief it derives from is marked [VERIFIED] (parts\research_india_commercial.md line 264), with the modelling instruction at line 278 followed exactly.

3. The failure scenario ("the developer will put a state dropdown on the invoice screen") is blocked by two acceptance checks the reviewer did not read. M17-29's own check: "Change the linked registration from one state to another; an invoice to a customer in the first state changes from an intra-state split to an inter-state single tax **automatically**." M1-62 (SPEC.md line 1391): "Raise an invoice for a customer in another state; the system produces Integrated GST **automatically**", with the same prohibition — "This must never be a checkbox a clerk ticks." A clerk-set state dropdown fails both checks.

4. The "own registration state is unconfirmed" point is already carried three times, not missed: OPEN-Q-B14 (line 1240), OPEN-Q-C1 (line 1393, which even instructs seeding the Karnataka registration **marked unconfirmed** and "Do not code either answer in"), and OPEN-Q-D18 (line 3861, "Everything about the tax split depends on this").

The proposed fix is also defective. (a) It would create `place_of_supply_state` as a new field that already exists, risking a duplicate of `place_of_supply_state_code`. (b) It routes a tax-field override to the **Approving Authority**, which in this document is the NABL technical report signatory (lines 476, 973, 2276) — the wrong role entirely; commercial authority here sits with Accounts / Lab In-Charge / Unit Incharge (lines 1461, 3843-area M17-43). (c) The proposed OPEN-Q asks whether a "performance-based rule" applies to testing goods at the laboratory. For domestic supplies there is no such entry in s.12 — the performance-based rule (s.13(3)(a)) only applies where supplier or recipient is outside India, and the research brief nowhere flags this. So the new open question would inject a false doubt into a point the brief records as settled.

Residual value, at most a Minor editorial tightening rather than a Major missing capability: M17-29 could add "…and the place of supply shall be a derived, read-only field on the invoice" to make the field-table convention (Derived/Auto/Read-only, used consistently at lines 1707-1711, 2049-2057, 2194-2205) explicit for the invoice, and could carry the Rule 50 proviso from parts\research_india_commercial.md line 282 (where rate or place of supply is not ascertainable at receipt of an advance, treat as 18% inter-State) into M17-32. Neither justifies a Major missing-capability finding.

rejectedForTheRecord.problem: The number-retained-on-cancellation rule is stated for money receipts and for nothing else. M17-36 permits a tax invoice to be cancelled before returns are filed and says nothing about what happens to its number; M17-37's gaps report has a "Cancelled" state, which implies retention but never requires it. A developer reading M17-17 in contrast with M17-36 can reasonably conclude that invoice numbers, unlike receipt numbers, are recycled on cancellation — which destroys the consecutive series M17-28 requires and turns the gaps report into a lie.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected: The finding rests on a factual error: the reviewer claims the number-retained-on-cancellation rule "is stated for money receipts and for nothing else." It is in fact stated as a global normative rule in Section 10.3 "Numbering rules" (parts/section_2_workflow.md:709ff; SPEC.md:1208ff), which the reviewer appears not to have read. WF-100 [MUST] (SPEC.md:1216) says: "A number is never reused. A cancelled document keeps its number, remains stored, remains searchable and remains printable, marked Cancelled," and its acceptance check is literally the invoice case the reviewer says is missing: "Cancel an invoice, then raise the next. The new invoice takes the following number, not the cancelled one." WF-99 [MUST] (SPEC.md:1215) lists the gap-free series (invoice, bill of supply, advance receipt voucher, refund voucher, credit note, money receipt, report, conditioning certificate, ULR, complaint, NCR) and its acceptance check is "Every number from 1 to the current counter is listed as Issued or Cancelled, and no number is reported Missing" — the reviewer's own desired outcome. WF-101 forbids deleting any numbered document at the database-grant level; WF-102 duplicates the Issued/Cancelled/Missing register with alerts. Every remaining clause of the proposed fix is also already present: "never renumber" in M20.6 rule 2 (SPEC.md:4229); "appears in its serial position marked cancelled" in M20-19 [MUST] (section_4_functional_support.md:1199, acceptance check "the register shows it as cancelled in its serial position") and M20-03; "remains stored as the frozen file" in M17-39 [MUST] and WF-113; reason/actor/timestamp on cancellation in NFR-102 [MUST] (SPEC.md:4956, reason "cannot be left blank" for numbered documents); and the failed-transaction void case in AC-31 (SPEC.md:5596, "never reused"). The same rule is restated per family for reports (SPEC.md:1178), complaints (:1191), equipment (:1188, M11-01), samples (WF-47) and allocations (WF-85). The alleged contrast is also a misreading: M17-17's "separate from the tax invoice series" is about series separation (the government money receipt is a different document from the tax invoice), not a carve-out; and M17-36 governs WHEN cancellation is permitted (before a return is filed), a different question from what happens to the number, which Section 10.3 answers once for all series. There is therefore no missing capability, no contradiction, and the proposed fix would create a fifth restatement of an already-stated MUST that must be kept in sync — and its absolute "for ever / never reissued" phrasing risks reading against WF-107, which deliberately allows a configured policy of reusing the original ULR on an amendment. At most this is a trivial cross-reference nicety (M17 could cite WF-99/WF-100 the way M20-12/M20-13 cite M17), not a Major gap.

rejectedForTheRecord.location: M16-03 (line 753); switch table `environment_limits` (line 1598)
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: Stated as settled fact, with no standard designation, no edition and no unverified marker — and it contradicts the only support in the research pack, which gives "27 ± 2 °C, 65 ± 4 % RH" for the standard atmosphere for testing textiles. The difference is not cosmetic: in the monitored, non-air-conditioned room OPEN-Q15 tells us to expect, ± 2 % will put almost every reading into the Excursion Register and every test into the withhold path of M16-09, while M16.4 rule 1 simultaneously warns against limits that make excursions meaningless. The scientist will take ± 2 % as established and will not know it was never verified.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
The finding's load-bearing factual claim is false. The reviewer says M16-03's "65 % ± 2 %" is an unverified assertion that "contradicts the only support in the research pack, which gives 65 ± 4 % RH". The research pack in fact verifies exactly the figure the spec states. parts/research_silk_domain.md:405 reads: "Winding, size, seriplane, serigraph, cohesion all require **65 ± 2% RH and 27 ± 2 °C**, with the sample conditioned to moisture equilibrium for **24 h** first. **[F, S4]** (Note: **27 °C**, the Indian variant — ISO/ASTM use 20 °C; IS 832-2:2011 explicitly says the 20 °C international figure *"is not suitable for Indian conditions"* **[F]**)". S4 (research_silk_domain.md:18) is the full text of IS 15090 Parts 1-11:2002 — the Indian Standard that actually governs raw silk testing and grading for this laboratory. It is corroborated at research_silk_domain.md:436 ([F, S4]) and at research_gap_analysis.md:127 and :345 ("in India commonly 27 ± 2 °C, 65 ± 2 % RH"). The reviewer's ±4 % appears exactly once in the whole pack, as a parenthetical "e.g." in a general-textile aside in research_nabl_17025.md:169, in the 17025 brief rather than the silk-domain brief, with no [F] marking. So the confidence check in step 5 comes out the opposite way from the finding: the spec states a [F]-verified, primary-source fact, and correctly carries no [U] marker. It also does hedge — "as used in India", "clearly labelled as the Indian variant", and the glossary at SPEC.md:374 says "commonly".

The mechanism argument is also wrong. M16-09 (SPEC.md:3684) creates the Nonconformity and the Withheld state on "an excursion outside a **method's** stated requirement", not outside the area default, and M16-04 gives the method version's requirement precedence over the area default. Because IS 15090 itself requires ±2 %, changing the area default to ±4 % would not move a single test out of the withhold path. The reviewer's invocation of M16.4 rule 1 backfires: that rule says "Do not set limits so wide that nothing is ever an excursion — that defeats the purpose", i.e. it argues against the proposed widening, not against the spec. OPEN-Q15 already tells the scientist to expect frequent excursions in a monitored, non-air-conditioned room and to make the excursion workflow "quick to complete rather than punitive", which is the concern the reviewer raises.

Every substantive element of the proposed fix is already in the document: "the tolerance shall not be hard-coded" is M16-02 ("Limits shall be data, not code, and changing them shall require a reason and remain in history") and M4-16 at SPEC.md:1849 ("held in the Method master as configuration, not in program code, with an effective date"); "take the tolerance from the conditioning standard each method cites" is M14-10 (SPEC.md:3374) plus M1-36 (SPEC.md:1340), which already stores "required standard atmosphere" and "required pre-conditioning hours" per method revision; and "print the standard designation next to the limit so it is defensible to an assessor" is M14-02 (designation + edition + amendment), M14-12 (result stores the method version; reports print designation, edition and amendment as at the date of test) and M8-06.

Finally, the fix would introduce new internal contradictions rather than remove one. Dropping to ±4 % would conflict with the glossary (SPEC.md:374), the IS 15090 (Part 5):2002 worked example (SPEC.md:784, "24 h conditioning at 27 ± 2 °C and 65 ± 2 % RH"), the M4-16 [MUST] (SPEC.md:1849), and the environment_limits switch default (SPEC.md:4523) — and would substitute a weaker figure for a verified one while adding a note that misdescribes the research pack. The only residual grain of truth is that M16-03 does not itself print an IS number beside the limit; given that the designation and edition are already mandated on the method version and on the report, that is a cosmetic nicety, not a Major unverified-fact defect.

rejectedForTheRecord.location: section_5_nfr_plan.md ARC-13 signing row (line 341), Phase 1 scope (line 641), Phase 6 (line 703), ARC-43 (line 407), AC-05 (line 829), go-live checklist item 3 (line 793)
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: Phase 1 ships only "the internal electronic signature" (a `sys_esign` row), yet AC-05 requires the Phase 1 PDF to be "rendered, stored, fingerprinted and signed", ARC-43 requires "Two key pairs ... from day one" with distinct key identifiers, AC-46 requires the public service to recognise a staging key identifier, and go-live checklist item 3 gates go-live on a "Production signing key generated, stored per ARC-38". Meanwhile the only three permitted implementations are a local key file marked development-only, an HSM with a Document Signer certificate that Phase 6 explicitly defers, and an e-sign service provider that would breach ARC-01/NFR-32 by putting an external call on the report-issue path. There is therefore no lawful way to sign a production report in Phase 1. Nowhere does the document say who obtains the CCA-licensed Document Signer certificate, in whose name, on what procurement lead time (compare the 6 weeks budgeted for safe-to-host in OPEN-Q-T3), or who physically holds the USB token when the Scientist-D is transferred — which ARC-38 itself lists as one of three unresolved storage options.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
The quote at parts/section_5_nfr_plan.md:341 is genuine, but the finding is a misreading that conflates three signing mechanisms the document deliberately keeps separate.

(1) Phase 1's "internal electronic signature" is tier (i)/(b) of a three-tier model defined twice: M8-46 (section_3_functional_core.md:1245) "a system electronic signature - an authenticated user, re-authenticated at the moment of signing, cryptographically bound to the file's checksum, with a tamper-evident audit record" and M21-43 (section_4_functional_support.md:1491), both naming that tier the minimum acceptable. NFR-39 - which AC-05 itself cites in its Verifies column - defines a complete report as having "its rendered file, its file fingerprint and its signature record". So AC-05's "signed" is discharged by the sys_esign record bound to pdf_sha256, not by PKI. AC-05 cites no PKI requirement at all (NFR-16, NFR-39, NFR-42, NFR-79, DB-13, DB-26).

(2) The signing key that ARC-38 to ARC-43, ARC-27, txn_report.signing_key_id and go-live item 3 govern is the QR payload key, not a certificate. M9-01/M9-02/M9-03 specify a self-generated elliptic-curve key pair with a key identifier in the payload header; M9-32 requires the public key published at a stable web address plus a printable fingerprint sheet - which is ARC-40 verbatim. ARC-42 is M9-35 verbatim. ARC-43 plus AC-46 (public service reports the staging key identifier as unknown) is the published-key list. No certifying authority is involved in this path at any point. ARC-38's FIRST listed storage option - "the operating-system key store" - is available in Phase 1 with nothing to procure, so go-live item 3 is fully satisfiable: generate an EC key pair, hold it in the OS key store, publish the public key, keep the ARC-27 test key out of production. This is essentially what the reviewer's proposed ARC-46 asks for, already present.

(3) The cryptographic PDF signature (PAdES / organisational Document Signer certificate) is ARC-13's row, M8-46 tier (ii)/(iii) and M21-43 tier (c). Phase 6 calls it "the STRONGER digital signature" - the comparative states that Phase 1 runs a weaker tier by design. The local key file therefore stays development-only and Phase 1 never needs it. There is no "unlawful production signing" state.

The document also never overstates the Phase-1 signature: M8-15 requires only that the report "identifies the person authorising it by name and designation - a printed identity, not merely a signature image", and no requirement prints a legal digital-signature claim before Phase 6's acceptance milestone. The reviewer's proposed report-face disclaimer solves a problem the document does not have.

The proposed fix would also introduce three new defects. (a) Re-labelling the local key file as "Phase 1 production" contradicts research_india_commercial.md:424, whose verdict is that self-signed PKCS#12 is acceptable "only as the internal integrity mechanism during development and for the internal tamper-evidence chain" and must never be presented to a customer as a legal signature. (b) It hard-codes a key identifier "DVM-K1" where M9-03 and ARC-40 deliberately keep identifiers configurable and rotatable. (c) "Procurement starts in Phase 0 and is budgeted at 8 weeks" is wrong on timing: Phase 0 is 2 weeks and Phase 6 begins at week 35 per the §26.1 cumulative column, while the research brief records Document Signer certificates as issued for 1, 2 or 3 years - a certificate obtained around week 10 would be most of the way through a one-year validity before its first use.

Residual nit, far below Blocker and not what was filed: the research brief's own open question ("Signing decision: is a CCA-licensed certificate budgeted for v1? ... Get two written CA quotes", research_india_commercial.md:867) is not carried into the OPEN-Q-T register, and no role is named as key custodian beyond ARC-38's "the organisation's custody" (ARC-44 does cover the passphrase as a documented, rotatable secret). That is a Phase-6 procurement question against a phase whose own text reads "Risk if skipped: none that is urgent" - a Minor register-completeness gap, not a missing Phase-1 capability.

rejectedForTheRecord.location: section_5_nfr_plan.md NFR-27 (line 85), NFR-29 (line 96), ARC-19 (line 361), ARC-22 (line 364), AC-23 (line 867)
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: NFR-27 requires the lab to "receive samples, test, verify, and print reports with a valid QR code" for five continuous working days with no internet, and ARC-19 makes the verification record reach the public service only by outbound queue. So for up to five days every freshly issued certificate carries a QR that the public service cannot answer — and ARC-22 mandates that this answer is indistinguishable from "no such report". A buyer at the cocoon market scanning a genuine certificate printed that morning gets the same page as a forgery, which is precisely the failure AC-23 says must never happen ("an error lets a forger claim the server is down"). Separately, NFR-27's target says five continuous working days and its own verification column says "Pull the internet cable for one full working day" — the test does not test the requirement.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected: The finding rests on a misreading of how the public page decides "genuine". It does not depend on the published record. section_3_functional_core.md M9-01/M9-02/M9-03 make the QR a SIGNED PAYLOAD (elliptic-curve signature, three-part compact format, key identifier in the header); M9-32 and ARC-40 publish the matching public keys at a stable address; and M9's own plain-language paragraph states the seal check "works with no internet connection at all... The internet is needed for one extra question only - 'has this report since been amended or withdrawn?'". A forger cannot mint a valid seal, so a forgery gets M9-17's "NOT GENUINE - the seal does not match" or "This is not a report verification code", while a genuine report printed during an outage gets "Signature verified". AC-23 (section_5_nfr_plan.md:867) is therefore not breached: the two answers are visibly different pages. AC-46 (:905) independently confirms the public service evaluates key identifiers on its own ("reports the staging key identifier as unknown"), i.e. seal evaluation is not gated on the outbound queue. The claimed ARC-22 contradiction also does not exist: ARC-22's identical-answer rule is scoped to '"not found" and "exists but not visible"' - the enumeration threat on bare report numbers, mirrored by M9-12/M9-13 and traceable to the [ASSUMPTION]-marked source at research_india_commercial.md:558 - and says nothing about a seal-verified scan. AC-23's own case (a SUPERSEDED report) has a published record by definition, since it was published at original issue. The eventual-consistency half is already handled: NFR-30 queues publication gracefully, NFR-31 drains it with retry, M9-40 states the internal system never depends on the public service being reachable, and AC-33 requires that "on reconnection the queue drains with no human action and the verification page then shows the day's reports". What genuinely remains is far smaller than a Blocker: M9-19's caveat wording attributes the unknown live status to the visitor's device ("no internet connection"), while the field-table trigger at section_3_functional_core.md:1486 is generic ("Shown when the status could not be checked"); and NFR-27's 5-working-day target is verified by a 1-day cable pull. Both are Minor wording/test-scope nits, not a contradiction, and neither produces the forgery-indistinguishable failure claimed. The proposed fix is also actively harmful: prose inside the QR payload violates M9-04 ("carries, and carries only" the enumerated fields) and M9-02's 30 mm phone-readability sizing; collapsing the page to three answers deletes M9-17's NOT GENUINE / "Unknown issuer key" / malformed-code states, M9-18's fifth state and contradicts NFR-69's required GENUINE / NOT GENUINE / SUPERSEDED / CANCELLED wording; printing "if this page reports the report as unknown, the record is still in transit" on the report face gives any forger a printed excuse and contradicts M9-37's trust anchor ("Verify only at (fixed address). Do not rely on any other link."); and the ARC-22 carve-out is self-cancelling because the fix's own third answer "never confirms or denies the existence of a report number", which is exactly what ARC-22 already mandates.

rejectedForTheRecord.location: section_5_nfr_plan.md Phase 1 requirement list (line 643), DB-13 (line 555), Phase 4 (line 679), AC-05 (line 829) vs section_2_workflow.md OPEN-Q12 (line 794), §10.2 (lines 754-764)
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: Four statements cannot all be true. Phase 1's requirement list includes "DB-01 to DB-42", i.e. the ULR template engine DB-13. rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
Quote is genuine, but the finding is already addressed and its factual half is wrong.

(1) ALREADY HANDLED — nine places state the conditional the reviewer says is absent, including verbatim the acceptance check he proposes to add as new AC-49. parts/section_3_functional_core.md:1590, M10-34: "Where the laboratory is accredited for this work, the Unique Laboratory Report number and the accreditation symbol apply on the same terms and with the same hard blocks as M8-27 to M8-35. Where it is not, neither prints." Acceptance check: "With the unit configured as non-accredited, no symbol and no such number print." Also M8-27 (line 1210) "Where the laboratory IS accredited and..."; M8-34 "Nothing in the report... may imply that work is accredited when it is not"; M8-35 symbol "suppressed automatically the moment accreditation validity lapses"; report field table line 1285 "Only where the whole report is in accredited scope | Blank otherwise"; public-page field table line 1467 "Absent for non-accredited work"; OPEN-Q6 (line 1221), which duplicates OPEN-Q12 with the identical not-accredited default; WF-106; the §10.1 ULR row; workflow step 18 (section_2_workflow.md:34).

(2) THE CLAIMED FAILURE IS PHYSICALLY BLOCKED — DB-27 is a database CHECK: CHECK ((ulr_no IS NULL AND nabl_symbol_used = false) OR contains_out_of_scope = false). With an empty accredited-scope master every report is out-of-scope, so the constraint forces ulr_no NULL. AC-05 would fail as a TEST; it cannot ship as a false accreditation claim. And AC-05 mentions only a ULR, not the accreditation symbol or any narrative claim, so "ends an accreditation assessment" is doubly overstated for a lab that by default has no accreditation to assess.

(3) THE §10.2 HALF IS FLATLY WRONG, and its fix would inject a falsehood. The reviewer quoted research_lims_reference.md:435 — the weaker secondary brief, which itself defers: NABL "published a new accreditation-certificate-number format and a revised ULR clarification in June/July 2026 — the developer must read the current NABL circular." research_nabl_17025.md IS that reading. §0 and §1.2 are built on the primary circular "Clarification regarding Unique Laboratory Report (ULR) Number, 11.06.2026 (rev. 15.06.2026)", quote it directly, link the nabl-india.org PDF, and give position-by-position tables with the identical worked examples the spec transcribes (NABLT0626MP200012600000001, TC115162600000042, TC47792600000042). §1.3 states the location digit and trailing F are gone — exactly the spec's "Any implementation copied from a pre-2026 article will be wrong." That brief's own "Items explicitly marked UNVERIFIED" list (line 776) contains the (I) suffix, the serial leading digit, discipline/group print order, dual QR and signature wording — NOT the three formats. The spec does not overstate; the proposed header would assert something the research pack contradicts and would blunt a correctly-sourced warning.

(4) TWO PREMISES ARE SHAKY. §27's preamble does not scope it to Phase 1 — it spans AC-26 (Phase 4) and AC-30 (Phase 2) — and Phase 1's own acceptance milestone (line 649) names no ULR, so "the Phase 1 happy path the lab signs off" is the reviewer's inference. "DB-01 to DB-42" is generically over-inclusive rather than a ULR-specific contradiction: it equally drags in DB-36/37/40 (invoice/tax, Phase 2) and DB-42 (QC, Phase 4).

"DB-01 to DB-12, DB-14 to DB-35, DB-41" silently drops DB-38 (sample disposal requires recorded authorisation) although Phase 1's Included list explicitly covers "sample retention, return and disposal", and it removes DB-13 while retaining DB-27 — the ULR/symbol guard — which is incoherent.

Residual after all this: AC-05's Given omits "in the accredited scope" and its Then says "a ULR" without "where applicable" — the same imprecision as NFR-79 (line 192). That is a missing-qualifier nit in one test row, fully governed by the normative layer, i.e. trivial, not a Blocker.

M6-44 then states the concurrency policy explicitly: "No merge or conflict resolution logic is required, because only one tester owns an allocation at a time" (section_3_functional_core.md:932 = SPEC.md:2177). Reading attribution is per-observation anyway (txn_observation.observed_by_personnel_id), never inherited from txn_worksheet.analyst_personnel_id, so the stated failure mode cannot occur.

(1) "no storage" is wrong. txn_sample_test already carries checked_by_personnel_id and checked_at, distinct from verified_by_personnel_id/verified_at, and there is no "Checked" state in the allocation state machine — those two columns are the Under Verification holder and pickup time, which is precisely what WF-75's acceptance check needs ("refused with the first verifier's name"). SPEC.md:1046 states the lock as the state's documented side effect ("Locks the record to that verifier so two people do not verify the same allocation"); DB-15 routes every state move through one service function that checks the rule exists; NFR-38 names "verification" as a documented transaction boundary. An abandoned lock also has human release routes: Unit Incharge is a listed actor on Under Verification, send-back and On Hold are permitted exits, and M7-40/WF-89 raise ageing alerts on the verification queue.

(3) is overstated on two of its three named categories. Results cannot be silently last-write-wins: M6-24 (a submitted reading can never be overwritten), M6-32 (a submitted result is locked to the tester), WF-72, DB-06 (revision pattern with mandatory reason), DB-33 (no UPDATE permission on txn_observation), M6-48 (an import must never silently overwrite), NFR-34/NFR-35/AC-35 (a reading already accepted by the server is never overwritten by a buffered copy). Reports cannot either: DB-07, DB-25 and AC-28 make an issued report immutable even against direct SQL. DB-04 additionally audits every field change with old and new value, so no mutable-row change is "silent".

The fix is also wrong. A per-line assigned_to_personnel_id with readings attributed to the line's tester directly contradicts M5-13 and both worksheet field validations. row_version on "every transaction table" is meaningless on txn_observation, where DB-33 grants no UPDATE permission. And the 4-hour auto-release is incoherent with this design: the lock IS the state, so releasing lock columns while DB-15 forbids any state write outside the transition function would leave the allocation permanently stuck in Under Verification and unclaimable by anyone.

Residual kernel, at most Minor: DB-15 does not say how the check-then-update in the transition function is made race-safe (whereas DB-08 spells out SELECT ... FOR UPDATE for the analogous numbering race), and there is no stated stale-write policy for the genuinely mutable rows that remain (draft sample registration, order lines, master data). That is a one-line clarification, not a Major missing capability, and §27 could gain a concurrency AC alongside AC-31.

rejectedForTheRecord.location: section_5_nfr_plan.md mst_equipment_correction (line 450), NFR-41 (line 115), DB-20 (line 562), DB-21 (line 563), DB-30 (line 579), AC-18 (line 857)
rejectedForTheRecord.problem: Calibration certificates arrive weeks after the calibration date; that is normal. Two consequences are unhandled. (1) `mst_equipment_correction` carries `effective_from`/`effective_to` and is "applied automatically by the calculation engine", but no correction factor is snapshotted onto `txn_observation` or `txn_result` and DB-21's snapshot list does not mention corrections. So loading a certificate with a backdated `effective_from` silently changes the value that NFR-41's regression suite recomputes — "Re-running the stored calculation on the stored raw readings, using the stored formula version, gives exactly the same reported value including rounding" becomes false for every affected historical result, and the software-validation evidence for ISO/IEC 17025 clause 7.11.2 fails on a release where no code changed. (2) DB-30 is a trigger on observation insert only. Entering an `mst_equipment_event` whose `valid_until` is earlier than previously assumed, or whose result is Fail, retroactively puts existing observations outside calibration validity with no detection at all — the AC-18 impact analysis is described as a screen the Unit Incharge opens, not as something the system fires when the certificate is entered.
rejectedForTheRecord.whyRejected:
Both limbs of the finding are already handled, and the reviewer's central factual assertions are contradicted by the document.

LIMB 1 ("no correction factor is snapshotted; NFR-41 regression and ISO/IEC 17025 7.11.2 evidence fail") is wrong. parts/section_3_functional_core.md line 884, M6-16 [MUST]: "Where the calibration certificate carries a correction factor, the current factor is applied automatically by the calculation engine, ITS VALUE IS STORED ON THE RESULT, and THE FACTOR'S VERSION IS RECORDED. Applying a stale factor must be impossible." Acceptance check: "Update a balance's correction factor; new results use the new factor and OLD RESULTS RETAIN THE OLD ONE." That is exactly the behaviour the reviewer asks to be added. Reinforced at section_3_functional_core.md line 960: "Correction factor applied | Derived | Auto | From the current calibration record | Read-only; version stored." M11-13 (section_4 line 40) makes factor selection date-of-observation based, with an acceptance check proving a 2027 observation does not pick up a 2026-valid factor. So a backdated effective_from cannot silently alter a stored result, NFR-41 does not become false, and no validation evidence fails. The reviewer's residual point is only that §25.2's txn_result row does not NAME a column for it — but that table's own header is "Key columns", not a complete DDL, and txn_result already carries formula_version plus intermediates_json for exactly this class of frozen calculation input. A schema table that does not enumerate every column required by a functional MUST is not a contradiction.

LIMB 2 ("retroactive equipment events go undetected; AC-18 is just a screen the user opens") is also wrong. M11-24 [MUST] (section_4 line 51) triggers on "a calibration fails, an intermediate check fails, a fault is reported that could affect results, OR A CALIBRATION IS DISCOVERED TO HAVE LAPSED", auto-proposes suspect_from as the last known-good check, lists every test/sample/worksheet/report/customer in the window by database query (M11-25), and requires each affected issued report to be dispositioned as "Not affected (with technical justification) / Retest / Amend report / Withdraw and replace" — verbatim the four options the reviewer's DB-47 proposes to add. It fires on entry, not on demand: M11-12's acceptance check (line 39) is "Record a Fail; the system IMMEDIATELY OFFERS to start an Impact Analysis (M11-24) and to move the instrument out of service"; M11-17 does the same for a failed intermediate check. The return-to-service block the reviewer wants already exists: equipment state table line 137 ("A Fail calibration event; Impact Analysis opened") and line 139 ("Out of service / Quarantined -> In service | Lab In-Charge | Re-verification record and, where relevant, A CLOSED IMPACT ANALYSIS"), plus M11-23. Edge case 3 (line 147) handles the exact "valid_until earlier than assumed" case: a discovered lapse "must [be treated] exactly like a failed calibration for the purpose of Impact Analysis: suspect_from defaults to the original due date, and every result produced after that date must be dispositioned." Edge case 4 handles per-range correction tables. Non-closure is escalated by alert IMPACT_OPEN (line 1089), and the output is persisted in txn_ncr_affected (section_5 line 505) with disposition, justification, actor and timestamp.

THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD ALSO INTRODUCE PROBLEMS. DB-47 duplicates M11-24 almost word for word and creates a second, competing mechanism (a "pending impact-analysis task" enforced by a database trigger) alongside the existing Nonconformity -> Impact Analysis -> txn_ncr_affected flow, with no statement of how the two relate — a real contradiction where none exists today. Its blanket "blocks the equipment from returning to service" also conflicts with the graduated state-transition table, which distinguishes Pass-with-correction (returns to service) from Fail (Impact Analysis opened), and would block return to service on the mere entry of a routine correction factor. The DB-30 amendment is the one marginally useful element, but DB-30 already says the trigger compares observed_at "against the equipment's valid-until dates" (plural, matching mst_equipment_event.valid_until), and M6-14 and M11-19 both state explicitly that the check is against the observation date and not today.

Residual value is editorial only, not Major and not a contradiction: DB-21's snapshot list could cross-reference the correction snapshot that M6-16 already mandates.
